+---
+title: Microsoft Entra resource policy concepts (preview)
+description: Understand policy definitions, versions, assignments, parameters, enforcement modes, and permissions in Microsoft Entra resource policy.
+ms.topic: concept-article
+ms.date: 11/11/2026
+ai-usage: ai-generated
+# Customer intent: As a tenant administrator, I want to understand the resource policy object model so that I can manage policies and assignments safely.
+---
+
+# Microsoft Entra resource policy concepts (preview)
+
+Microsoft Entra resource policy separates the logic that identifies noncompliant requests from the assignment that controls where and how that logic applies. This article explains the shared concepts used across the Microsoft Entra admin center and Microsoft Graph.
+
+## Policy definitions
+
+A policy definition describes a configuration requirement and the requests to which it applies.
+
+- A **built-in policy** provides Microsoft-managed, read-only logic that you can assign without authoring Rego. Use the `builtInDefinitions` collection to discover available definitions and versions.
+- A **custom policy** contains Rego that you author and manage.
+
+A custom definition has a `uniqueName` that identifies it across versions. Its Rego package uses `graph.<uniqueName>["X.Y.Z"]` to identify the name and version. Metadata describes the policy, and `__metadata__.selector` identifies its target resource type or action and operations.
+
+Creating a definition doesn't enforce it. Create and enable an assignment to evaluate matching requests.
+
+## Policy versions
+
+Custom policy definitions start at `1.0.0` and use semantic versions in the `X.Y.Z` format. Updating the policy source publishes a higher version, and the former current version becomes an immutable previous version. A parameter schema change requires a major version increase.
+
+Each assignment references a specific definition and version, including assignments of built-in policies. Select an exact available version; publishing a newer version doesn't automatically update existing assignments.
+
+Keep policy code and its change history in source control. Service-maintained version history isn't a substitute for a source repository.
+
+For update, rollback, and retirement procedures, see [Update and retire resource policies](resource-policy-lifecycle.md).
+
+## Policy assignments
+
+A policy assignment connects a policy to a scope and provides its runtime settings. The assignment's `assignedPolicy` reference identifies a custom or built-in definition by `policyUniqueName` and a specific `version`.
+
+Each definition version can have one live assignment per tenant. A live assignment is one that hasn't been soft-deleted; disabled assignments count too. Update the existing assignment to change its parameters or enforcement settings.
+
+| Setting | Purpose |
+| --- | --- |
+| `uniqueName` | Identifies the assignment. The name can't be changed after creation. |
+| `scope` | Identifies the assignment scope. Tenant-wide scope is represented by `/`. |
+| `isEnabled` | Controls whether the assignment participates in evaluation. |
+| `enforcementMode` | Controls whether a noncompliant result blocks the request. |
+| `params` | Supplies typed values for the policy's parameters. |
+
+For custom definition and assignment names, choose a `uniqueName` that starts with an ASCII letter, contains only ASCII letters, digits, or underscores, and has at most 128 characters. The prefixes `microsoft` and `ms`, including `msft`, are reserved regardless of case. The exact custom definition names `utils` and `input` are also reserved regardless of case. For example, use `contosoApplicationNaming` rather than a Microsoft-reserved prefix.
+
+Multiple assignments can match a request. Review all applicable assignments when investigating a blocked operation.
+
+## Enforcement modes and enablement
+
+Enablement and enforcement mode control different behavior.
+
+| Assignment state | Behavior |
+| --- | --- |
+| Disabled | The assignment doesn't participate in policy evaluation. |
+| Enabled with `doNotEnforce` | The policy evaluates matching requests and records results without blocking them through this assignment. |
+| Enabled with `enforce` | A noncompliant result from this assignment can block the request. |
+
+Use `doNotEnforce` to assess impact before enforcing a policy. It isn't an exception to a different enforced assignment.
+
+## Parameters
+
+Parameters let you reuse policy logic with different values, such as a required naming prefix.
+
+Custom definitions declare parameter types and defaults in `__metadata__.paramsSchema`; assignments supply values in `params`. For validation rules, Rego references, and examples, see [Resource policy parameters](resource-policy-parameters.md).
+
+## Applicability and exceptions
+
+The required `__metadata__.selector` identifies matching resource types or actions and operations. An optional `applicable` rule can further narrow which requests a custom policy evaluates. For selector syntax and derived-type behavior, see [Applicability metadata](resource-policy-rego.md#applicability-metadata).
+
+Use parameters and applicability logic to express narrowly defined exceptions when the policy supports them. An exception excludes a request from that policy; it doesn't grant permission to perform the operation or bypass other policies.
+
+Review exception ownership, scope, and continued need as part of [safe deployment](resource-policy-safe-deployment.md).
+
+## Roles and API permissions
+
+Microsoft Entra roles and Microsoft Graph API permissions serve different purposes. In a delegated API workflow, the client needs the required delegated permissions, and the signed-in user needs the role required for the operation. Application-only workflows use application permissions.
+
+| Role | Intended tasks |
+| --- | --- |
+| Resource Policy Administrator | Manage definitions and assignments, and evaluate policies. |
+| Resource Policy Reader | Read definitions and assignments, and inspect policy behavior. |
+| Resource Policy Evaluator | Evaluate policy logic without policy management permissions. |
+| Reports Reader | Read [evaluation audit events](resource-policy-logs.md). |
+
+The following Microsoft Graph API permissions cover resource policy tasks and are available as delegated and application permissions:
+
+| API permission | Intended tasks |
+| --- | --- |
+| `ResourcePolicyDefinition.Read.All` | Read built-in and custom definitions, versions, and deleted custom definitions. |
+| `ResourcePolicyDefinition.ReadWrite.All` | Read and manage custom definitions and versions, including restoring or permanently deleting definitions. |
+| `ResourcePolicyAssignment.Read.All` | Read assignments, including deleted assignments. |
+| `ResourcePolicyAssignment.ReadWrite.All` | Read and manage assignments, including restore and permanent deletion. |
+| `ResourcePolicyEvaluation.Read.All` | Test inline or assigned policies with `evaluatePolicy` and `evaluateAssignedPolicies`. |
+| `ResourcePolicyConfiguration.Read.All` | Read tenant configuration and retrieve the federated identity credential subject. |
+| `ResourcePolicyConfiguration.ReadWrite.All` | Read and update tenant configuration, including the privileged-read application. |
+| `AuditLog.Read.All` | Read [evaluation audit events](resource-policy-logs.md). |
+
+Use standard role assignment and consent experiences. Choose the least-privileged role and API permissions for each task. Policy management access doesn't grant access to the resources used in a test operation.
+
+Real additional reads through `fetchAsPolicy()` use a [configured privileged-read application](resource-policy-privileged-read-app.md). Running those reads through `evaluatePolicy` also requires `ResourcePolicyDefinition.ReadWrite.All` and, for delegated access, a role that can manage definitions.
+
+## Delete and restore
+
+Deleting a custom definition or assignment follows a soft-delete lifecycle. Restore dependencies in order: restore the definition before an assignment that references it.
+
+Deleting an individual previous definition version is different: that operation is permanent. For retention, dependency checks, and irreversible operations, see [Update and retire resource policies](resource-policy-lifecycle.md).
+
+## Related content
+
+- [What is Microsoft Entra resource policy?](resource-policy-overview.md).
+- [How resource policy evaluation works](resource-policy-evaluation.md).
+- [Author resource policies with Rego](resource-policy-rego.md).
+- [Safely deploy resource policy assignments](resource-policy-safe-deployment.md).

+---
+title: How Microsoft Entra resource policy evaluation works (preview)
+description: Understand request matching, Rego evaluation, enforcement modes, multiple assignments, and propagation of resource policy changes.
+ms.topic: concept-article

+# Customer intent: As a tenant administrator, I want to understand policy evaluation so that I can interpret results and safely enable enforcement.
+---
+
+# How Microsoft Entra resource policy evaluation works (preview)
+
+Microsoft Entra resource policy evaluates matching Microsoft Graph requests before the requested resource operation proceeds. Evaluation combines assignment settings with the assigned policy's applicability and compliance rules.
+
+## Request-time evaluation
+
+Evaluation has three stages.
+
+1. **Match assignments.** The service finds enabled assignments whose scope, target resource or action, and operations match the incoming request. If none match, resource policy doesn't evaluate Rego for the request.
+1. **Check applicability.** If the assigned policy has an `applicable` rule, the service evaluates it. A false result excludes the request from that policy's compliance evaluation.
+1. **Evaluate compliance.** The service evaluates each applicable policy's `deny` rule. A true result identifies noncompliance; a false result identifies compliance.
+
+The service combines the results with assignment enforcement modes to determine whether resource policy blocks the request.
+
+## Multiple policies and enforcement modes
+
+An assignment's `enforcementMode` doesn't change the policy's compliance result. It changes how the service applies that result.
+
+| Results | Request-time behavior |
+| --- | --- |
+| At least one applicable policy returns a noncompliant result through an `enforce` assignment. | Resource policy blocks the request. |
+| Noncompliant results occur only through `doNotEnforce` assignments. | Those assignments don't block the request, and evaluation results are recorded. |
+| All applicable policies evaluate successfully and are compliant. | Resource policy doesn't block the request. |
+
+An excluded or compliant result from one policy doesn't override a different enforced policy's noncompliant result.
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> Passing policy evaluation doesn't guarantee that the underlying operation succeeds. Microsoft Graph permissions, resource validation, and other service controls still apply.
+
+## Disabled assignments and exceptions
+
+A disabled assignment doesn't evaluate requests. An enabled assignment in `doNotEnforce` mode evaluates without enforcing its result.
+
+An exception expressed in a policy's applicability logic affects only that policy. It doesn't grant Microsoft Graph permissions or bypass other assignments.
+
+## Simulated evaluation
+
+Use evaluation actions to test policy behavior without performing the simulated resource operation.
+
+| Action | What it evaluates |
+| --- | --- |
+| `evaluatePolicy` | Rego supplied directly in the evaluation request, with any supplied parameter values. |
+| `evaluateAssignedPolicies` | Assigned policies that match the simulated request. |
+
+Inspect policy results and errors even when the evaluation returns HTTP success. Success alone doesn't prove compliance.
+
+Both actions return `appliedPoliciesEffects` and `isBlocked`. A noncompliant result can have `appliedPoliciesEffects: "deny"` and `isBlocked: false` when it isn't enforced. For `evaluatePolicy`, supply `enforcementMode` to test the intended behavior; its default is `doNotEnforce`. For `evaluateAssignedPolicies`, the assignments supply their enforcement modes.
+
+Request detailed results with `isResultDetailed: true` to inspect policy-provided violation reasons separately from evaluation errors.
+
+For testing guidance, see [Test and troubleshoot a resource policy](resource-policy-test-troubleshoot.md).
+
+## Assignment propagation
+
+Assignment creation, updates, and deletion can take up to 10 minutes to affect incoming requests. The evaluation actions and policy management APIs reflect saved assignment changes without that propagation delay.
+
+Account for propagation when testing enablement, enforcement-mode changes, version changes, or rollback. An immediate management response doesn't prove that every incoming request uses the updated assignment.
+
+## Errors and diagnostics
+
+Distinguish a noncompliant policy result from a loading or evaluation failure. Failures can arise from invalid Rego, unexpected input, unavailable policy versions, or unsuccessful additional reads.
+
+Review per-policy results and available error details. Don't assume that an evaluation error is equivalent to a deny result.
+
+| Condition | Request-time behavior |
+| --- | --- |
+| An applicable policy's `deny` evaluation fails or returns an undefined result. | An `enforce` assignment blocks the request. A `doNotEnforce` assignment records the error without blocking through that assignment. |
+| An optional `applicable` rule fails or returns an invalid result. | That policy doesn't proceed to `deny` evaluation. Other matching policies can still block the request. |
+| The request payload exceeds the policy evaluation input-size limit. | Policy evaluation is skipped. A matching enforced deny assignment blocks the request; assignments in `doNotEnforce` don't block through this size check. |
+| An unexpected service error prevents policy evaluation from completing. | The request can continue without completed policy evaluation. A successful write isn't proof that all policies evaluated successfully. |
+
+For additional reads, the policy must inspect the `fetchAsPolicy()` response code. A failed read isn't automatically a noncompliant result; the policy's handling of that response determines whether it returns a result or encounters an evaluation error.
+
+Use [evaluation audit logs](resource-policy-logs.md) to investigate real requests. Inspect the assignment and version in each event: a request's overall decision can differ from an individual assignment's result. These logs don't assess preexisting resource configuration.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Resource policy concepts](resource-policy-concepts.md).
+- [Author resource policies with Rego](resource-policy-rego.md).
+- [Test and troubleshoot a resource policy](resource-policy-test-troubleshoot.md).
+- [Safely deploy resource policy assignments](resource-policy-safe-deployment.md).

+---
+title: Export Microsoft Entra resource policy logs (preview)
+description: Configure optional diagnostic export for resource policy evaluation logs and use Kusto queries to analyze them in Log Analytics.
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 11/11/2026
+ai-usage: ai-generated
+# Customer intent: As a tenant administrator, I want to export resource policy evaluation logs so that I can run custom queries or send the logs to another monitoring system.
+---
+
+# Export Microsoft Entra resource policy logs (preview)
+
+Export resource policy evaluation logs to Log Analytics for KQL queries, Azure Storage for archival, or Azure Event Hubs for downstream processing.
+
+For direct request investigation or assignment assessment, use the [Microsoft Graph evaluation audit-log API](resource-policy-logs.md). Export is optional.
+
+The queries summarize exported requests, not tenant-wide resource compliance. Azure destinations can incur separate charges.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- A Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 tenant license for log export.
+- A work or school account with an active [Security Administrator](~/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#security-administrator) role in the Microsoft Entra tenant to configure diagnostic settings in the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
+- An Azure subscription with an existing destination. For the KQL workflow, use a [Log Analytics workspace](/azure/azure-monitor/logs/quick-create-workspace) that you can select as the destination. An Event Hubs-only export doesn't require a workspace.
+- For KQL queries in the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com), the [Log Analytics Reader](/azure/role-based-access-control/built-in-roles/monitor#log-analytics-reader) role on the destination workspace. Microsoft Entra roles don't grant Azure workspace access. For access options, see [Manage access to log data and workspaces](/azure/azure-monitor/logs/manage-access).
+- An enabled policy assignment and representative requests that match its resource type and operations.
+
+If you access Log Analytics through the Microsoft Entra admin center instead of the Azure portal, also use the [Reports Reader](~/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#reports-reader) role. See [Analyze activity logs with Log Analytics](~/identity/monitoring-health/howto-analyze-activity-logs-log-analytics.md).
+
+Activate any eligible roles through Privileged Identity Management (PIM) before starting.
+
+## Configure log export
+
+Create the diagnostic setting for the Microsoft Entra tenant, not an application or policy. These steps configure Log Analytics:
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) in the tenant whose policies you want to monitor.
+1. Browse to **Entra ID** > **Monitoring & health** > **Diagnostic settings**.
+1. Select **Add diagnostic setting**.
+1. Enter a name, such as `resource-policy-evaluations`.
+1. Under **Logs**, select **MicrosoftGraphPolicyLogs**. Selecting **MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs** alone doesn't export policy evaluation details.
+1. Under **Destination details**, select **Send to Log Analytics workspace**.
+1. Select the destination subscription and workspace, and then select **Save**.
+1. Reopen the setting and verify that the category is enabled and the intended workspace is selected.
+
+For other destinations, follow [Configure Microsoft Entra diagnostic settings](~/identity/monitoring-health/howto-configure-diagnostic-settings.md) or [Stream logs to an event hub](~/identity/monitoring-health/howto-stream-logs-to-event-hub.md). For automation, use the tenant-scoped [diagnostic settings resource](/azure/templates/microsoft.aadiam/2017-04-01/diagnosticsettings), not a workspace diagnostic setting.
+
+If the category isn't available, confirm that resource policy log export is enabled for your preview tenant. Don't substitute a different category.
+
+Use the column names shown here for Log Analytics. The Microsoft Graph API uses different property names.
+
+## Verify that evaluations arrive
+
+1. Make an approved request that matches an enabled assignment. Record the UTC time and request ID. A write can change directory data.
+1. In the Azure portal, open the destination **Log Analytics workspace**, select **Logs**, and use KQL mode.
+1. Run the following query with your Microsoft Entra tenant ID. Once records arrive, [find your recorded request](#investigate-a-specific-request) to confirm it was exported.
+
+```kusto
+let targetTenantId = "<tenant-id>";
+MicrosoftGraphPolicyLogs
+| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
+| where AadTenantId == targetTenantId
+| summarize Evaluations = count(), LastEvaluation = max(TimeGenerated)
+```
+
+Use `AadTenantId`, not the workspace's `TenantId`. See the [table reference](/azure/azure-monitor/reference/tables/microsoftgraphpolicylogs) for column definitions.
+
+Allow for [export and ingestion delay](~/identity/monitoring-health/howto-configure-diagnostic-settings.md#basic-process). If no rows appear, check the tenant, destination, time range, and enabled assignment. Requests outside enabled assignments don't produce policy evaluation records; no rows isn't proof of compliance.
+
+## Analyze outcomes over time
+
+1. Replace `<tenant-id>` and adjust the time range for your observation period.
+1. Run this query to compare decisions over time and count requests with errors separately:
+
+```kusto
+let targetTenantId = "<tenant-id>";
+MicrosoftGraphPolicyLogs
+| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
+| where AadTenantId == targetTenantId
+| summarize Requests = count(),
+    RequestsWithErrors = countif(ErrorPoliciesCount > 0)
+    by bin(TimeGenerated, 1h), PolicyDecision
+| order by TimeGenerated desc
+```
+
+A `deny` decision means blocked. Nonblocking outcomes can use `audit` or `none`; inspect `PolicyDetails` to distinguish violations from errors. Don't count every `none` result as a violation.
+
+## Assess one assignment's impact
+
+1. Enter the tenant and assignment names, and choose a time range covering representative traffic.
+1. Run this query to separate violations from loading, applicability, and evaluation errors.
+1. Use the caller `AppId` and request details to work with affected application owners on remediation or supported temporary exceptions. Follow [safe deployment](resource-policy-safe-deployment.md) before enabling enforcement.
+
+```kusto
+let targetTenantId = "<tenant-id>";
+let assignmentName = "<assignment-unique-name>";
+MicrosoftGraphPolicyLogs
+| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
+| where AadTenantId == targetTenantId
+| mv-expand PolicyDetail = PolicyDetails
+| where tostring(PolicyDetail.assignmentUniqueName) == assignmentName
+| extend IsApplicable = tobool(PolicyDetail.isApplicable),
+    IsCompliant = tobool(PolicyDetail.isCompliant),
+    HasError = isnotempty(tostring(PolicyDetail.policyLoadingError))
+        or isnotempty(tostring(PolicyDetail.applicabilityEvaluationError))
+        or isnotempty(tostring(PolicyDetail.evaluationError))
+| summarize MatchedRequests = count(),
+    ApplicableRequests = countif(IsApplicable),
+    NoncompliantRequests = countif(IsApplicable and IsCompliant == false and HasError == false),
+    RequestsWithErrors = countif(HasError)
+    by AppId, RequestMethod, TargetResourceName
+| order by NoncompliantRequests desc
+```
+
+These are selected-assignment results, not the overall enforcement decision. Another assignment can block the same request. `PolicyDetails` can be truncated, so counts reflect retained details, not necessarily all evaluations.
+
+## Investigate a specific request
+
+1. Replace the tenant and request placeholders. If you recorded only the client-supplied identifier, filter on `ClientRequestId` instead of `RequestId`.
+1. Run the query and inspect `PolicyDetails` for the assignment, version, reasons, and errors.
+
+```kusto
+let targetTenantId = "<tenant-id>";
+let targetRequestId = "<request-id>";
+MicrosoftGraphPolicyLogs
+| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
+| where AadTenantId == targetTenantId
+| where RequestId == targetRequestId
+| extend MatchingAssignments = toint(column_ifexists("EvaluatedPoliciesCount",
+    column_ifexists("PolicyDetailsCount", int(null))))
+| project TimeGenerated, RequestId, ClientRequestId, OperationId,
+    RequestMethod, RequestUri, AppId, PolicyDecision,
+    MatchingAssignments, ErrorPoliciesCount, PolicyDetails
+```
+
+`MatchingAssignments` uses the available count column. A null count means unknown, not zero; don't substitute the length of a potentially truncated `PolicyDetails` array.
+
+For batch children, filter on the parent's `OperationId`; each child has its own `RequestId`. To correlate with [Graph activity logs](/graph/microsoft-graph-activity-logs-overview), enable `MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs` separately and match `RequestId` and `OperationId`.
+
+For a diagnostic checklist, see [Test and troubleshoot a resource policy](resource-policy-test-troubleshoot.md).
+
+## Protect evaluation data
+
+Limit access to exported logs and follow your organization's retention requirements. Don't put credentials or unnecessary personal data in policy messages.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Analyze resource policy evaluation audit logs](resource-policy-logs.md).
+- [How resource policy evaluation works](resource-policy-evaluation.md).
+- [Safely deploy resource policy assignments](resource-policy-safe-deployment.md).

+---
+title: Update and retire Microsoft Entra resource policies (preview)
+description: Publish a new policy version, try it alongside an enforced version, switch enforcement, roll back, and delete or restore resource policies.
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 11/11/2026
+ai-usage: ai-generated
+# Customer intent: As a policy administrator, I want to update or retire a policy so that I can preserve existing protection and recovery options.
+---
+
+# Update and retire Microsoft Entra resource policies (preview)
+
+Use this article to update an assigned policy, roll back, or delete and restore policies. Assess a new version through a separate report-only assignment while the existing version stays enforced.
+
+For your first policy assignment, testing, and enforcement readiness, see [Safely deploy resource policy assignments](resource-policy-safe-deployment.md). For parameter-value changes, see [Edit an assignment](resource-policy-manage-portal.md#edit-an-existing-assignment) and [Parameter update behavior](resource-policy-parameters.md#assignment-update-behavior).
+
+Use [Microsoft Graph Explorer](https://developer.microsoft.com/graph/graph-explorer) to call the linked Microsoft Graph APIs for these procedures. For portal assignment controls, see [Manage policies in the Microsoft Entra admin center](resource-policy-manage-portal.md).
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- A work or school account in the target tenant with active [Resource Policy Administrator](resource-policy-concepts.md#roles-and-api-permissions) and [Reports Reader](~/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#reports-reader) roles. Use Resource Policy Administrator for policy management and evaluation, and Reports Reader for evaluation audit events.
+- [Microsoft Graph Explorer](https://developer.microsoft.com/graph/graph-explorer), signed in to that tenant with the same account, with admin consent for the delegated permissions listed below. Request only the permissions for the procedures you follow.
+- A Microsoft Entra ID Governance service plan for publishing or updating policies, creating or updating assignments, and restoring deleted items. See [licensing requirements and exceptions](licensing.md#resource-policy-preview).
+- A policy or assignment to update, retire, or restore. For the parallel rollout below, the existing assignment must be enabled and enforced.
+- A saved copy of the current policy and assignment settings, including parameter values.
+- For policies that use `fetchAsPolicy()`, a [configured privileged-read application](resource-policy-privileged-read-app.md) with application permissions for the Microsoft Graph reads used by the policy.
+
+Activate any eligible roles through Privileged Identity Management (PIM) before signing in to Graph Explorer.
+
+| Delegated permission for Graph Explorer | When needed |
+| --- | --- |
+| `ResourcePolicyDefinition.ReadWrite.All` | Publish, delete, or restore custom definitions, or manage their versions. Not needed for assignment-only changes to built-in policies. |
+| `ResourcePolicyAssignment.ReadWrite.All` | Read, create, update, delete, or restore assignments. |
+| `ResourcePolicyEvaluation.Read.All` | Test policy changes. |
+| `AuditLog.Read.All` | Review evaluation audit events. |
+
+## Publish a new custom policy version
+
+For a built-in policy, select an available newer version and go directly to [Roll out the new version](#roll-out-the-new-version). Don't edit built-in definitions.
+
+1. Update your Rego policy and increase its version number. Update any parameter reference or import to match the new package version. For example, change `1.0.0` to `1.1.0` in the package declaration:
+
+    ```rego
+    package graph.application_name_prefix["1.1.0"]
+    ```
+
+1. [Test the revised policy](resource-policy-test-troubleshoot.md) with the intended parameter values and requests that should pass and fail. Check that unchanged requirements still behave as expected.
+1. [Update the custom definition](/graph/api/resourcepolicydefinition-update?view=graph-rest-beta&preserve-view=true) with the revised Rego, following the API reference's update requirements.
+1. Confirm that both versions are available. Keep your existing assignment unchanged.
+
+A parameter schema change requires a higher major version, such as `2.0.0`, and compatible parameter values. Keep the target resource type unchanged. See [Author policies with Rego](resource-policy-rego.md).
+
+## Roll out the new version
+
+Use two assignments: one enforces the old version, and the other evaluates the new version in report-only mode.
+
+Each version can have only one live assignment in a tenant, including a disabled assignment. Choose a new version that isn't already assigned; don't repoint the existing assignment to it.
+
+1. [Create a new assignment](/graph/api/resourcepolicyassignment-create?view=graph-rest-beta&preserve-view=true) with a different name, the new policy version, and its intended parameter values. Set it to enabled (`isEnabled: true`) and report-only (`enforcementMode: doNotEnforce`). Leave the existing enforced assignment on.
+1. Wait for [assignment changes to take effect](resource-policy-evaluation.md#assignment-propagation).
+1. Confirm that evaluation audit events include both assignment names and their expected policy versions.
+1. [Review the new assignment's impact](resource-policy-logs.md#assess-assignment-impact-from-evaluation-events), agree on remediation or supported temporary exceptions, and complete the [checks before enforcement](resource-policy-safe-deployment.md#6-enable-enforcement).
+1. [Update the new assignment](/graph/api/resourcepolicyassignment-update?view=graph-rest-beta&preserve-view=true) to **Enforce** (`enforcementMode: enforce`). Keep the old assignment enforced while the change takes effect.
+1. Verify the new assignment's enforced results in evaluation audit events, and test compliant and noncompliant requests.
+1. Once the new version is enforcing as expected, turn the old assignment **Off** (`isEnabled: false`). Keep that assignment and its policy version available for rollback.
+
+Review each assignment's results separately. The old version can still block requests that the new one would allow. While both versions enforce, either can block.
+
+## Roll back to the previous version
+
+To return to the old version, use the assignment you retained:
+
+1. Check that the old assignment still references the tested version and has its original parameter values.
+1. Turn the old assignment **On** with **Enforcement** set to **Enforce**.
+1. Wait for [assignment changes to take effect](resource-policy-evaluation.md#assignment-propagation).
+1. Verify the old assignment's enforced results in evaluation audit events and test requests.
+1. Turn the new assignment **Off** after the old assignment is enforcing again.
+
+This order keeps enforcement in place. Don't create another assignment for a version that already has one.
+
+Rollback doesn't undo resource changes that were already allowed.
+
+## Retire an old version
+
+Keep the old version and assignment until you no longer need them for recovery.
+
+1. Confirm that the replacement works and the policy owner approves retirement.
+1. [Delete the old assignment](/graph/api/resourcepolicyassignment-delete?view=graph-rest-beta&preserve-view=true). A disabled assignment still prevents you from deleting its policy version.
+1. For a custom policy, [delete the unused previous version](/graph/api/resourcepolicydefinitionversion-delete?view=graph-rest-beta&preserve-view=true). Don't delete Microsoft-managed built-in versions.
+
+> [!WARNING]
+> Deleting a previous version is permanent. It can't be restored.
+
+Keep custom policy source in your own repository. See [Version-history limits](resource-policy-service-limits.md#version-history-and-deleted-items).
+
+## Delete a custom policy
+
+To remove a custom policy you no longer need:
+
+1. Save its Rego and assignment settings if you might need them later.
+1. Delete all assignments that reference the definition, including disabled assignments.
+1. [Delete the custom definition](/graph/api/resourcepolicydefinition-delete?view=graph-rest-beta&preserve-view=true).
+
+Deleted definitions and assignments can be restored for 30 days. Permanent deletion or expiration removes this recovery option.
+
+## Restore a deleted policy or assignment
+
+Restore the policy before an assignment that uses it:
+
+1. [Restore the custom definition](/graph/api/resourcepolicydefinition-restore?view=graph-rest-beta&preserve-view=true) if it was deleted, and confirm that the required version is available.
+1. Review the deleted assignment's version, parameters, and enablement and enforcement settings.
+1. Confirm that the version has no other live assignment, including a disabled assignment.
+1. [Restore the assignment](/graph/api/resourcepolicyassignment-restore?view=graph-rest-beta&preserve-view=true).
+1. Allow the restored settings to take effect, then verify request behavior and evaluation audit events.
+
+Restore the deleted assignment rather than reusing its reserved name.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Create and manage resource policies in the Microsoft Entra admin center](resource-policy-manage-portal.md).
+- [Safely deploy resource policy assignments](resource-policy-safe-deployment.md).
+- [Analyze resource policy evaluation audit logs](resource-policy-logs.md).
+- [Resource policy parameters](resource-policy-parameters.md).

+---
+
+# Analyze Microsoft Entra resource policy evaluation audit logs (preview)
+
+Use [Microsoft Graph Explorer](https://developer.microsoft.com/graph/graph-explorer) to investigate a policy decision or identify applications affected by an assignment. You don't need diagnostic export or a Log Analytics workspace to retrieve these events. Logs describe evaluated requests, not the compliance of every preexisting resource.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- A tenant where resource policy preview is available. For assignment-impact queries, record the assignment's unique name. See [resource policy licensing requirements](licensing.md#resource-policy-preview).
+- A work or school account in the target tenant with an active [Reports Reader](~/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#reports-reader) role.
+- [Microsoft Graph Explorer](https://developer.microsoft.com/graph/graph-explorer), signed in to that tenant with the same account, with admin consent for the delegated `AuditLog.Read.All` permission.
+- Representative traffic after assignment changes propagate.
+
+Personal Microsoft accounts aren't supported. `ResourcePolicyEvaluation.Read.All`, used to test policies, doesn't grant access to audit events.
+
+If your role is eligible through Privileged Identity Management (PIM), activate it before signing in to Graph Explorer.
+
+## Retrieve evaluation audit events
+
+Use evaluation audit events to investigate an individual request.
+
+By default, queries return events from the past 24 hours. Filter on `evaluatedDateTime` to specify a different window. The examples use `ge` and `le` to include both the start and end times.
+
+1. Sign in to Graph Explorer with the account described in [Prerequisites](#prerequisites), and select **GET** and **beta**.
+1. Record the operation's UTC time and response `request-id` or the `client-request-id` you supplied.
+1. Filter on `requestId` to retrieve the matching event and its policy details. Replace the placeholder with the recorded identifier and the timestamps with a UTC window that includes the operation:
+
+    ```http
+    GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/auditLogs/resourcePolicy?$filter=requestId eq '{request-id-or-client-request-id}' and evaluatedDateTime ge 2026-11-06T09:00:00Z and evaluatedDateTime le 2026-11-06T18:00:00Z&$select=id,requestId,appId,evaluatedDateTime,policyDecision,policyDetails
+    ```
+
+1. Select **Run query**. In **Response preview**, review `policyDecision` and the matching assignment in `policyDetails`. Check the policy version, `policyMessage`, and any loading or evaluation errors.
+
+`policyDecision` describes the overall request: `deny` means blocked, `compliant` means no violations or errors were found, and `none` means nonblocking noncompliance or errors. A successful request doesn't prove policy compliance.
+
+If no event appears, allow for logging delay and check the time window, tenant, assignment propagation, and read permissions. For error investigation, see [Test and troubleshoot a resource policy](resource-policy-test-troubleshoot.md).
+
+## Assess assignment impact from evaluation events
+
+Keep a new assignment in report-only mode while assessing it. For a version update, leave the old assignment enforced and follow [Roll out the new version](resource-policy-lifecycle.md#roll-out-the-new-version).
+
+1. Record the new assignment's unique name and introduction time. Choose an end time that covers representative traffic after [assignment changes take effect](resource-policy-evaluation.md#assignment-propagation).
+1. In Graph Explorer, use **GET** and **beta** to query the assignment's events. Replace the assignment name and timestamps with your observation window:
+
+    ```http
+    GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/auditLogs/resourcePolicy?$select=id,appId,evaluatedDateTime,policyDecision,policyDetails&$filter=policyDetails/any(c:c/assignmentUniqueName eq '{unique-assignment-name}') and evaluatedDateTime ge 2026-11-06T09:00:00Z and evaluatedDateTime le 2026-11-06T18:00:00Z&$count=true
+    ```
+
+1. Select **Run query**. Follow `@odata.nextLink` if returned to retrieve the remaining pages.
+1. Use `appId` to identify caller applications. In each event, review the selected assignment's version, `isApplicable`, `isCompliant`, `policyMessage`, and errors. An applicable, noncompliant result without errors indicates a violation; investigate errors separately.
+1. Work with application owners to update their applications or plan supported temporary exceptions. Repeat the query after changes, and follow [safe deployment](resource-policy-safe-deployment.md) before enabling enforcement.
+
+Don't filter report-only assessment to `policyDecision eq 'deny'`: that would exclude nonblocking violations. An overall deny can come from another enforced assignment. Missing events or incomplete details don't prove compliance.
+
+The examples show spaces for readability. URL-encode query values when sending requests.
+
+## Optional diagnostic export
+
+For custom KQL queries, archival, or integration with other monitoring systems, see [Export resource policy logs](resource-policy-export-logs.md). Export is optional and isn't required for Graph access.
+
+## Protect evaluation data
+
+Limit access to evaluation events and follow your organization's retention requirements. Policy messages and request context can contain sensitive information.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Quickstart: Assign a built-in resource policy](resource-policy-quickstart-portal.md).
+- [How resource policy evaluation works](resource-policy-evaluation.md).
+- [Safely deploy resource policy assignments](resource-policy-safe-deployment.md).
+- [Export resource policy logs](resource-policy-export-logs.md).

+---
+title: Create and manage Microsoft Entra resource policies in the admin center (preview)
+description: Manage resource policy definitions, assignments, versions, deleted items, and privileged-read configuration in the Microsoft Entra admin center.
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 11/11/2026
+ai-usage: ai-generated
+# Customer intent: As a tenant administrator, I want to manage policies in the Microsoft Entra admin center so that I can govern resource changes without writing management scripts.
+---
+
+# Create and manage Microsoft Entra resource policies in the admin center (preview)
+
+Use the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com/) to find built-in policies, manage custom definitions and assignments, and configure privileged policy reads.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- A tenant where resource policy preview is available.
+- A Microsoft Entra ID Governance service plan for operations that require a license. See [licensing requirements and exceptions](licensing.md#resource-policy-preview).
+- A work or school account with an active [Resource Policy Administrator](resource-policy-concepts.md#roles-and-api-permissions) role in the intended tenant. Use this account in the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com/) for policy, assignment, and configuration management. If the role is eligible through Privileged Identity Management, activate it before performing management tasks.
+- To set or replace the privileged-read application, an application prepared by following [Configure the application](resource-policy-privileged-read-app.md#configure-the-application), including its federated identity credential and consented Microsoft Graph application permissions.
+
+For read-only access, use the [Resource Policy Reader](resource-policy-concepts.md#roles-and-api-permissions) role. A read-only role doesn't grant policy management access. These portal procedures don't require you to grant permissions to Graph Explorer.
+
+If management actions are unavailable because your role couldn't be verified, confirm it's active and select **Retry role check**. Operations that don't require a license still require management authorization.
+
+## Find resource policies
+
+1. Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center and confirm that you're in the intended tenant.
+1. Go to **Tenant governance**.
+
+Under **Resource policies**, choose the page for your task:
+
+| Page | Use it to |
+| --- | --- |
+| **Definitions** | Find policies and open their properties, assignments, and versions. |
+| **Assignments** | Review and manage assignments across the tenant. |
+| **Deleted items** | Review, restore, or permanently delete deleted definitions and assignments. |
+
+The tenant-wide **Assignments** page is separate from the **Assignments** tab on an individual policy definition.
+
+You can also use the resource policy shortcuts under **Overview** > **Get started** > **Prevent non-compliant resources** to open **Definitions** or **Assignments**.
+
+For tenant-wide configuration, open **Tenant governance settings** under **Settings**, then select **Resource policies**. See [Manage resource policy configuration](#manage-resource-policy-configuration).
+
+## Select a built-in policy
+
+Built-in policies let you apply a policy without writing Rego. Review a policy's requirements and supported resources before assigning it.
+
+1. In **Tenant governance**, select **Definitions**.
+1. On the **Built in** tab, find and select a policy. For example, select **Require a department prefix for application names**.
+1. On **Properties**, review the description and **Resource**.
+1. Note the **Unique name** and **Latest version** for the assignment.
+
+The example policy requires application names to start with an allowed department prefix and contain no banned words.
+
+Built-in definition properties and Rego content are read-only. Use the definition's **Assignments** tab to review its assignments and **Versions** tab to review version information.
+
+For the first-run workflow, see [Quickstart: Assign a built-in resource policy](resource-policy-quickstart-portal.md).
+
+## Create a custom definition
+
+Prepare and test the Rego before creating a custom definition. Creating a definition alone doesn't enable enforcement.
+
+1. Prepare a nonempty `.rego` file that follows the [required policy structure](resource-policy-rego.md#required-policy-structure). Include the policy name and version in the package declaration, and descriptive information, applicability, and any parameter schema in `__metadata__`.
+1. In **Tenant governance**, select **Definitions** and the **Custom** tab.
+1. Select **New definition**.
+1. In **Create resource policy definition**, select **Choose file** under **Rego policy file**, and select your `.rego` file.
+1. Confirm the selected file. Use **Replace file** or **Remove file** if you selected the wrong one.
+1. Select **Create**. Correct any validation or publication error before retrying.
+1. After the success message, return to **Definitions** > **Custom** and open the definition. Confirm its **Unique name**, **Latest version**, description, resource, and Rego content.
+
+Upload a complete `.rego` file; there's no inline editor. The policy source supplies the definition's name, description, and version.
+
+For policies that use `fetchAsPolicy()`, [configure the privileged-read application](#manage-resource-policy-configuration) before uploading. See [Author resource policies with Rego](resource-policy-rego.md) and [Test and troubleshoot a resource policy](resource-policy-test-troubleshoot.md).
+
+## Create or update an assignment
+
+Before changing an assignment, review its settings and follow [safe assignment deployment](resource-policy-safe-deployment.md).
+
+| Setting | Review |
+| --- | --- |
+| Assignment identifier | Identify the assignment you intend to change. |
+| **Version** | Confirm the policy version referenced by the assignment. |
+| **Status** | **On** enables evaluation. **Off** assignments aren't evaluated, regardless of enforcement mode. |
+| **Enforcement** | **Report-only** evaluates and records results without blocking requests. **Enforce** applies the deny effect and blocks noncompliant requests. |
+| **Parameters** | Review the values required by the selected policy version. A policy without configurable parameters doesn't require parameter entry. |
+
+Status and enforcement are independent. To assess a policy without blocking requests, use **Status** set to **On** and **Enforcement** set to **Report-only**.
+
+An existing assignment's identifier, policy definition, and version are read-only in **Edit**. To use a different policy version, create another assignment for that version; don't try to repoint the existing assignment.
+
+### Create an assignment
+
+You can start from the tenant-wide **Assignments** page or from a policy definition.
+
+1. In **Tenant governance**, select **Assignments** > **Create assignment**. Alternatively, open a definition and select **Add assignment** to use that definition.
+1. On **Settings**, enter an **Assignment identifier**, such as `contoso_application_naming`. Use a unique identifier that follows the [assignment naming rules](resource-policy-rego.md#required-policy-structure).
+1. If you started from the tenant-wide page, select **Select definition**, choose the intended policy in **Select policy definition**, and select **Select**.
+1. Confirm the **Version**. If multiple versions are available, choose the one you tested. A single available version can appear as read-only text.
+1. Set **Status** to **On** and **Enforcement** to **Report-only** for an initial deployment.
+1. Select **Next**. On **Parameters**, enter the values required by that version. For lists, use the [list parameter editor](#edit-a-list-parameter).
+1. Correct any validation errors, then select **Next**.
+1. On **Review**, confirm the policy, version, identifier, status, enforcement, and parameter values.
+1. Select **Add assignment**. Wait for **Resource policy assignment saved.**
+1. Open the saved assignment and confirm its settings.
+
+Assignments created in this workflow are tenant-wide (`/`); there's no scope selector.
+
+Each definition version can have only one live assignment, including an **Off** assignment. Already assigned versions and versions with unsupported parameter settings aren't available. If a version becomes unavailable while you're creating an assignment, select another version or review the existing assignment.
+
+If **Add assignment** can't check version availability, select **Retry checking available policy versions**. After the check succeeds, select **Add assignment** again.
+
+For an example configuration, see [Quickstart: Assign a built-in resource policy](resource-policy-quickstart-portal.md#1-select-a-built-in-policy-and-assign-it-in-your-tenant).
+
+### Edit an existing assignment
+
+Open an assignment from its policy definition to review or change its settings.
+
+1. In **Tenant governance**, select **Definitions** and open the policy.
+1. On **Assignments**, open the assignment.
+1. On **Assignment details**, review the version, status, enforcement, and parameters, then select **Edit**.
+1. On **Settings**, choose the **Status** and **Enforcement** values you need.
+1. Select **Next**.
+1. On **Parameters**, review and change the values you need. Strings and numbers use input fields; Boolean parameters use **True** or **False**. Optional Boolean parameters can be **Not configured**. Lists use a separate editor.
+1. Correct validation errors, then select **Next**.
+1. On **Review**, confirm the settings and parameter values, then select **Save**.
+1. Wait for **Resource policy assignment saved.**
+1. Reopen **Assignment details** and confirm the status, enforcement, version, and parameter values.
+
+If another administrator changes the assignment before you save, select **Refresh latest saved values**. Compare them with your draft on **Review**, select **I reviewed the latest saved values**, and save only if the settings are correct. Resolve any verification errors before resubmitting.
+
+Saved changes aren't necessarily effective on resource requests immediately. Allow for [assignment propagation](resource-policy-evaluation.md#assignment-propagation) and verify request behavior separately.
+
+### Edit a list parameter
+
+Some policies use lists of values. For example, **Require a department prefix for application names** uses `allowed_departments` for case-sensitive name prefixes.
+
+1. On **Parameters**, select **Edit allowed_departments**.
+1. In **Edit allowed_departments**, enter one value per row. Use **Add row** for another value, or **Remove** for a row you don't need.
+1. Correct any validation errors, then select **Apply** to update the assignment draft. To discard the list edits, select **Cancel**.
+1. Back on **Parameters**, select **Next**, review the assignment, and select **Save** for an existing assignment or **Add assignment** for a new one.
+
+For this example, optional `banned_word_list` and `client_appid_exclusion_list` lists can remain empty. Review each parameter's description before changing its values.
+
+**Apply** doesn't save the assignment to the service. Required lists can't be empty, and each value must match the type declared by the policy. For parameter semantics and defaults, see [Resource policy parameters](resource-policy-parameters.md).
+
+### Turn off an assignment
+
+Turn off an assignment when you want to stop evaluation without deleting its settings.
+
+1. Open **Assignment details** and select **Turn off**.
+1. Wait for **Resource policy assignment turned off.**
+1. Reopen the assignment and confirm **Status** is **Off**.
+
+You can also select **Edit**, set **Status** to **Off** on **Settings**, and complete **Parameters** > **Review** > **Save**. **Turn off** from assignment details saves directly; it doesn't use the edit wizard.
+
+If the portal reports that turning off succeeded but the saved status couldn't be verified, select **Check assignment status again**. This checks the saved state without repeating the change.
+
+An **Off** assignment still counts as that version's live assignment. To enable it again, use **Edit**, set **Status** to **On**, confirm the enforcement mode and parameters, and save. Allow for [assignment propagation](resource-policy-evaluation.md#assignment-propagation).
+
+## Delete an assignment
+
+Delete an assignment when you no longer want it to apply the policy. Removing an assignment doesn't require deleting the built-in policy definition.
+
+1. In **Tenant governance**, select **Assignments** to open **Resource policy assignments**.
+1. Select the checkbox for the assignment you want to delete. Confirm that only the intended assignment is selected, including any selections hidden by the current filter.
+1. Select **Delete**.
+1. In **Remove assignment?**, confirm **Selected items: 1.**, then select **Delete**.
+1. Confirm the status message: **Delete assignments: 1 succeeded; 0 failed.**
+
+The assignment moves to **Deleted items** and can be restored for 30 days. Allow for [assignment propagation](resource-policy-evaluation.md#assignment-propagation) before expecting resource requests to reflect the deletion.
+
+## Manage policy versions
+
+Custom policy versions and assignments have distinct lifecycles. Publishing a new custom version doesn't automatically move an assignment to it.
+
+### Review and download a version
+
+1. In **Definitions**, open the policy.
+1. Select **Versions** to review the current and previous versions.
+1. Select **Refresh** to reload the definition and its version history when you need the latest saved information.
+1. Select a version number to open its read-only policy source.
+1. Use **Download Rego** for the version you want to save.
+
+Use the assignment's version, not just the definition's **Latest version**, when investigating behavior or planning a rollback.
+
+If a download fails, retry **Download Rego** for the intended version.
+
+### Publish a new custom version
+
+You can't publish changes to Microsoft-managed built-in definitions.
+
+1. Save a copy of the current Rego and assignment settings.
+1. Revise and test the `.rego` file. Keep the definition's unique name and increase the package version as described in [Publish a new custom policy version](resource-policy-lifecycle.md#publish-a-new-custom-policy-version).
+1. In **Definitions** > **Custom**, open the definition.
+1. On **Properties**, select **Upload new version**.
+1. In **Upload policy version**, select **Choose file** and choose the revised `.rego` file.
+1. Confirm the file and select **Publish**. Correct any publication error before retrying.
+1. After the success message, reopen the definition and confirm **Latest version**, the uploaded policy source, and the previous version in **Versions**.
+
+Uploading identical content doesn't publish another version. If publication succeeds but you can't view the saved definition, refresh and check its version and source before uploading again.
+
+Create a separate assignment to test the new version in report-only mode. Keep existing protection in place during rollout. For rollout and rollback steps, see [Update and retire resource policies](resource-policy-lifecycle.md).
+
+## Delete a custom definition
+
+Save the Rego and assignment settings you might need for recovery before deleting a custom policy. Built-in definitions can't be deleted.
+
+1. Open the custom definition's **Assignments** tab and delete every live assignment that references it, including assignments whose status is **Off**.
+1. Return to **Definitions** > **Custom**.
+1. Select the checkbox for the intended definition, then select **Delete**.
+1. In **Delete this custom definition?**, review the selection and select **Delete**.
+1. Confirm the operation's status and check **Deleted items** > **Definitions**.
+
+Deleted custom definitions can be restored for 30 days unless permanently deleted first.
+
+## Restore deleted items
+
+Review the deleted item's settings before restoring it. Restoring an assignment can resume policy evaluation and enforcement with its saved settings.
+
+1. In **Tenant governance**, select **Deleted items**.
+1. If the custom definition was deleted, select the **Definitions** tab. Open the intended item's details to confirm its identity, then select its checkbox in the list and select **Restore**.
+1. If you restored a custom definition, return to **Definitions** > **Custom** and confirm that the required version is available.
+1. In **Deleted items** > **Assignments**, open the intended assignment's details. Review its definition, version, status, enforcement, and parameters.
+1. Confirm that no other live assignment, including an **Off** assignment, already uses that definition version.
+1. Select the deleted assignment's checkbox and select **Restore**.
+1. Return to **Assignments**, open the restored assignment, and confirm its saved settings.
+
+Restore a deleted definition before its assignments. Allow the restored settings to take effect, then verify request behavior and [evaluation audit events](resource-policy-logs.md). For reserved names and recovery requirements, see [Update and retire resource policies](resource-policy-lifecycle.md#restore-a-deleted-policy-or-assignment).
+
+## Permanently delete deleted items
+
+> [!WARNING]
+> Permanent deletion can't be undone. You can't restore a permanently deleted definition or assignment.
+
+1. In **Tenant governance**, select **Deleted items**.
+1. Select **Assignments** or **Definitions** for the item type.
+1. Select only the intended items, then select **Permanently delete**.
+1. In **Permanently delete selected items?**, confirm the selected-item count and select **Permanently delete**.
+1. Review the result and confirm that the items no longer appear in the deleted-items list.
+
+For operations on multiple items, review both the succeeded and failed counts. Partial success doesn't mean every selected item changed. Review the per-item errors and retry only the failed items.
+
+## Manage resource policy configuration
+
+The **Resource policies** tab in **Tenant governance settings** manages the tenant-wide resource policy configuration. Under **Privileged reads**, you can set, replace, or clear the application used by policies that call `fetchAsPolicy()`.
+
+### Set or replace the privileged-read application
+
+Prepare the application before saving its ID. This settings page doesn't register an application, create its federated identity credential, or grant Microsoft Graph permissions.
+
+1. Follow [Configure the application](resource-policy-privileged-read-app.md#configure-the-application) to prepare a customer-owned application, its federated identity credential, and consent for the required read permissions. Record its application (client) ID, not its application object ID or service principal object ID.
+1. In **Tenant governance**, under **Settings**, open **Tenant governance settings**.
+1. Select **Resource policies** and find **Privileged reads**.
+1. In **Privileged-read application (client) ID**, enter the application's client ID as a GUID. For a replacement, replace the existing value with the prepared application's client ID.
+1. Select **Save** and wait for **Privileged-read application settings were saved.**
+1. Reopen the **Resource policies** tab and confirm the intended client ID is saved. Resolve any saved-state verification warning before making another change.
+1. [Validate a live privileged read](resource-policy-privileged-read-app.md#validate-a-live-privileged-read) before relying on policies that use this application.
+
+For first-time setup, have one administrator configure this tenant-wide setting at a time.
+
+**Cancel** discards unsaved edits and returns the field to its loaded value. Saving the application ID doesn't prove that the application has all the read permissions your policies require.
+
+### Clear the privileged-read application
+
+> [!WARNING]
+> Clearing this setting disables privileged reads tenant-wide and affects every policy that uses `fetchAsPolicy()`. Review dependent policies and how they handle failed reads before proceeding.
+
+1. Open **Tenant governance settings** > **Resource policies**.
+1. Clear **Privileged-read application (client) ID** so the field is blank, then select **Save**.
+1. Reopen the tab and confirm the field is blank.
+
+Clearing the field doesn't delete the application or its credentials.
+
+### Recover from configuration errors
+
+Follow the message for the failed operation rather than repeatedly selecting **Save**.
+
+| Message or situation | Action |
+| --- | --- |
+| Settings couldn't be loaded. | Select **Retry loading settings**. |
+| Settings changed elsewhere. | Select **Refresh saved settings**. Compare **Current saved application ID** with your retained draft, then select **Save** only if you intend to replace the saved value. |
+| The saved settings or their version couldn't be verified. | Select **Refresh saved settings**. Don't submit another change until verification succeeds. |
+
+## Review evaluation results
+
+Use Graph Explorer for [simulated evaluations in the quickstart](resource-policy-quickstart-portal.md#2-validate-without-performing-a-write); these actions aren't available in the admin center. For real requests and enforcement tests, follow the [observe-and-enforce tutorial](resource-policy-tutorial-portal.md).
+
+To inspect real request outcomes and assess assignment impact, see [Analyze resource policy evaluation audit logs](resource-policy-logs.md).
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Resource policy concepts](resource-policy-concepts.md).
+- [Resource policy parameters](resource-policy-parameters.md).
+- [Analyze resource policy evaluation audit logs](resource-policy-logs.md).

+---
+title: What is Microsoft Entra resource policy (preview)?
+description: Learn how Microsoft Entra resource policy evaluates Microsoft Graph requests to help prevent noncompliant resource configuration changes.
+ms.topic: overview
+ms.date: 11/11/2026

+# Customer intent: As a tenant administrator, I want to understand resource policy so that I can prevent configuration changes that don't meet my organization's requirements.
+---
+
+# What is Microsoft Entra resource policy (preview)?
+
+Microsoft Entra resource policy helps you prevent configuration changes that don't meet your organization's requirements. You assign policies in your tenant, and the service evaluates matching Microsoft Graph requests before the requested changes occur.
+
+Resource policy is a feature of Microsoft Entra Tenant Governance. You can adopt it in an individual tenant without enabling related tenant discovery or establishing a governance relationship.
+
+## Prevent noncompliant changes
+
+Use resource policy to express configuration requirements for [supported resource types and actions](resource-policy-supported-resources.md). For example, a policy can evaluate a resource name or restrict a configuration value.
+
+A policy assignment controls how the service handles a noncompliant request:
+
+- In `doNotEnforce` mode, the policy evaluates the request and records the result without blocking it.
+- In `enforce` mode, a noncompliant result can block the request and return a policy-specific explanation.
+
+Another assignment in `enforce` mode can still block a request evaluated in `doNotEnforce` mode.
+
+Resource policy evaluates matching requests. Assigning a policy doesn't automatically scan or remediate preexisting resources, and it doesn't replace the permissions required to perform a Microsoft Graph operation.
+
+## Start with a built-in policy
+
+Built-in policies let you apply predefined requirements without writing policy code. Select a policy, supply its required parameters, and assign it in your tenant.
+
+Start with the [built-in policy quickstart](resource-policy-quickstart-portal.md) to assign and test a policy with simulated requests. Then follow the [tutorial to observe and enforce the policy](resource-policy-tutorial-portal.md) with real requests. Assess its impact in `doNotEnforce` mode before you enforce it.
+
+## Author a custom policy
+
+If a built-in policy doesn't meet your needs, author a custom policy in Rego, the declarative policy language used by Open Policy Agent. Define which requests the policy evaluates and the requirements they must meet.
+
+The policy's `deny` rule identifies noncompliance. The assignment's enforcement mode determines whether that result blocks the request.
+
+Learn about [resource policy parameters](resource-policy-parameters.md), [authoring with Rego](resource-policy-rego.md), and [managing policy versions](resource-policy-lifecycle.md).
+
+## Choose a management method
+
+Use the management method that fits your workflow.
+
+| Method | Use |
+| --- | --- |
+| Microsoft Entra admin center | Discover policies and manage definitions and assignments through the [admin center experience](resource-policy-manage-portal.md). |
+| Microsoft Graph REST APIs | Integrate policy management, simulated evaluation, and evaluation audit-log retrieval with your tools. |
+
+Keep Rego, tests, and assignment configuration in source control for review and repeatable API-based management.
+
+## Assess impact before enforcement
+
+Use simulated evaluations to test policy behavior without performing the requested write. Then use `doNotEnforce` assignments and the Microsoft Graph policy evaluation audit-log API to understand the impact on real requests. Inspect per-assignment results to identify noncompliance, affected applications and operations, and evaluation errors.
+
+The preview provides evaluation audit events, not service-generated aggregated impact reports. Diagnostic settings aren't required to retrieve events through Microsoft Graph. For the assessment workflow and optional custom analysis, see [Analyze resource policy evaluation audit logs](resource-policy-logs.md).
+
+Follow [safe assignment deployment practices](resource-policy-safe-deployment.md) before enabling enforcement.
+
+## Compare Tenant Governance features
+
+Tenant Governance features address different parts of your governance workflow.
+
+| Feature | Purpose |
+| --- | --- |
+| Related tenants | Discover tenants with observable relationships to your tenant. |
+| Governance relationships | Establish approved cross-tenant administrative access. |
+| Configuration management | Compare existing resource configuration with a baseline and report drift. |
+| Resource policy | Evaluate matching requests and help prevent noncompliant configuration changes. |
+| Secure tenant creation | Create add-on tenants with governance and recovery capabilities. |
+
+Use [configuration management](configuration-management.md) to detect configuration drift and resource policy to help prevent supported changes that would introduce noncompliance. Their supported resources and permissions aren't necessarily the same.
+
+## Licensing and availability
+
+Most resource policy operations during preview require a Microsoft Entra ID Governance service plan. See [Tenant Governance licensing](licensing.md#resource-policy-preview) for requirements and exceptions.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Resource policy concepts](resource-policy-concepts.md).
+- [How resource policy evaluation works](resource-policy-evaluation.md).
+- [Quickstart: Assign a built-in resource policy](resource-policy-quickstart-portal.md).
+- [Safely deploy resource policy assignments](resource-policy-safe-deployment.md).

+---
+title: Microsoft Entra resource policy parameters (preview)
+description: Understand resource policy parameter schemas, assignment values, defaults, validation, and update behavior.
+ms.topic: concept-article
+ms.date: 11/11/2026
+ai-usage: ai-generated
+# Customer intent: As a policy author or administrator, I want to understand parameter schemas and values so that I can configure reusable policy logic correctly.
+---
+
+# Microsoft Entra resource policy parameters (preview)
+
+Parameters separate reusable policy logic from assignment-specific values. A custom policy declares its parameter schema in `__metadata__.paramsSchema`; an assignment supplies values in `params`. Rego reads those values through a fully qualified reference or an import alias.
+
+Built-in policies define their own parameter schemas. You can set their assignment values, but can't edit their schemas.
+
+## Parameter schema
+
+The schema defines parameter names, types, descriptions, required values, and optional defaults. This fragment of `__metadata__` declares a required string, an optional Boolean, and an optional string array:
+
+```json
+{
+  "paramsSchema": {
+    "properties": {
+      "required_prefix": {
+        "type": "string",
+        "description": "Required prefix for application display names."
+      },
+      "case_sensitive": {
+        "type": "boolean",
+        "description": "Whether name comparisons are case-sensitive.",
+        "default": true
+      },
+      "banned_word_list": {
+        "type": "array",
+        "items": {
+          "type": "string"
+        },
+        "description": "Words the policy disallows in application display names.",
+        "default": []
+      }
+    },
+    "required": [
+      "required_prefix"
+    ]
+  }
+}
+```
+
+The schema describes configuration, not the policy's enforcement logic. For example, the string type permits an empty prefix; Rego must enforce a nonempty-prefix requirement if the policy needs one.
+
+## Assignment values
+
+Values belong in the assignment's `params` property:
+
+```json
+{
+  "params": {
+    "required_prefix": "Contoso-",
+    "case_sensitive": false,
+    "banned_word_list": [
+      "Test",
+      "Temp"
+    ]
+  }
+}
+```
+
+This assignment overrides the default `case_sensitive` value. When creating an assignment, omitting `case_sensitive` uses `true`, and omitting `banned_word_list` uses an empty array. Updates follow the [merge rules](#assignment-update-behavior) instead.
+
+These fragments aren't complete policy or assignment requests. For assignment procedures, see [Create or update an assignment](resource-policy-manage-portal.md#create-or-update-an-assignment).
+
+## Parameters in Rego
+
+In Rego, read parameter values through `data.graph.<definitionUniqueName>["<version>"].params`. The definition name and version must match the policy's package declaration.
+
+Import that path as `params` to keep rule expressions short:
+
+```rego
+package graph.application_name_prefix_parameterized["1.0.0"]
+
+import data.graph.application_name_prefix_parameterized["1.0.0"].params as params
+
+prefix := params.required_prefix
+case_sensitive := params.case_sensitive
+banned_words := params.banned_word_list
+```
+
+Without the alias, the prefix reference is `data.graph.application_name_prefix_parameterized["1.0.0"].params.required_prefix`. The import changes only Rego access; assignment and evaluation request bodies still use the JSON property `params`.
+
+Don't declare your own `params` rule. For the complete policy structure and rule requirements, see [Author resource policies with Rego](resource-policy-rego.md).
+
+## Validation and defaults
+
+The service validates values against the policy version's schema when creating or updating an assignment. Required parameters must have values, and supplied values must match their declared types. Optional parameters can have a `default` of the declared type; required parameters can't.
+
+`evaluatePolicy` also validates supplied `params` against the inline policy's schema, independently of assignments. It can check proposed values before an assignment changes. See [Test and troubleshoot a resource policy](resource-policy-test-troubleshoot.md#evaluate-custom-policy-logic).
+
+Parameter validation failures are configuration errors, not successfully evaluated policy violations. Passing schema validation doesn't prove that a resource change meets the policy's requirements.
+
+## Supported parameter types
+
+| Value | Schema example |
+| --- | --- |
+| String | `{"type": "string"}` |
+| Integer | `{"type": "integer"}` |
+| Number | `{"type": "number"}` |
+| Boolean | `{"type": "boolean"}` |
+| Array of strings | `{"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}` |
+
+Arrays contain scalars: `string`, `integer`, `number`, or `boolean`.
+
+Object values, nested arrays, nullable types, type unions, references, and schema composition aren't supported. Express constraints such as `enum`, `pattern`, `minLength`, and numeric bounds in Rego.
+
+Don't add root `type`, `$schema`, or `additionalProperties` keywords to `paramsSchema`.
+
+## Parameter names
+
+Names must start with an ASCII letter and contain only ASCII letters, digits, or underscores. `required_prefix` and `prefix1` are valid; `_prefix`, `1prefix`, and `required-prefix` aren't.
+
+Rego v1 reserved words can't be names: `as`, `contains`, `default`, `else`, `every`, `false`, `if`, `import`, `in`, `not`, `null`, `package`, `some`, `true`, and `with`.
+
+These rules apply even to unused declarations or values accessed with brackets.
+
+## Assignment update behavior
+
+Updates merge `params` with stored values. Supplied arrays replace stored arrays; they don't append.
+
+| Update | Behavior before schema validation and defaults |
+| --- | --- |
+| Omit `params` | Keep the stored values when the assigned version is unchanged. |
+| `"params": {}` | Keep the stored values. |
+| `"params": {"required_prefix": "Fabrikam-"}` | Replace this value and keep other stored values. |
+| `"params": {"required_prefix": null}` | Remove this stored value. |
+| `"params": null` | Clear all stored values. |
+
+After merging, the service validates values and applies defaults. Removing an optional value can restore its default. Removing a required value, such as `required_prefix`, fails validation.
+
+Because updates merge values, supplying the previous object alone doesn't remove newly added stored values. Restoring an earlier configuration also requires removing those additions with `null`.
+
+Only one live assignment is allowed per version, including a disabled assignment. Different parameter values can't be assessed through a second report-only assignment to the same version.
+
+For editing steps, see [Edit an existing assignment](resource-policy-manage-portal.md#edit-an-existing-assignment). Allow [assignment changes to take effect](resource-policy-evaluation.md#assignment-propagation) before interpreting request results.
+
+## Schema and version changes
+
+Changing the schema or logic requires a new definition version. A schema change requires a higher major version, such as `2.0.0`. See [Publish a new custom policy version](resource-policy-lifecycle.md#publish-a-new-custom-policy-version).
+
+Update parameter references or imports to match the new package version. Remove obsolete stored values with `null` members in `params`, and supply new required values in the same object.
+
+If you change `assignedPolicy.version`, explicitly include `params` and check that the resulting values meet the new schema. For rollout without losing existing enforcement, see [Roll out the new version](resource-policy-lifecycle.md#roll-out-the-new-version).
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Author resource policies with Rego](resource-policy-rego.md).
+- [Test and troubleshoot a resource policy](resource-policy-test-troubleshoot.md).
+- [Update and retire resource policies](resource-policy-lifecycle.md).
+- [Safely deploy resource policy assignments](resource-policy-safe-deployment.md).
+- [Create and manage resource policies in the Microsoft Entra admin center](resource-policy-manage-portal.md).
