+---
+title: Configure a privileged-read app for Microsoft Entra resource policy (preview)
+description: Configure and maintain a customer-owned application for read-only Microsoft Graph calls from resource policies that use fetchAsPolicy.
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 11/11/2026
+ai-usage: ai-generated
+# Customer intent: As a policy administrator, I want to configure least-privileged policy reads so that policies can evaluate related resource state without relying on caller read access.
+---
+
+# Configure a privileged-read app for Microsoft Entra resource policy (preview)
+
+Follow these steps to let resource policies read Microsoft Graph data through `fetchAsPolicy()`, independently of the caller's permissions. For function details, see [Read additional Microsoft Graph data](resource-policy-rego.md#read-additional-microsoft-graph-data).
+
+The trust values below apply to the global service. Confirm resource policy availability and trust values before using another cloud.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- An existing single-tenant application registration and its service principal in the target tenant.
+- A work or school member account in that tenant that owns the application registration and has an active [Resource Policy Administrator](resource-policy-concepts.md#roles-and-api-permissions) role. Application ownership lets you manage its federated identity credential without a tenant-wide application administrator role. See [Create a federated identity credential](/graph/api/federatedidentitycredential-post).
+- [Microsoft Graph Explorer](https://developer.microsoft.com/graph/graph-explorer), signed in to that tenant with this account, with admin consent for the delegated `Application.ReadWrite.All` and `ResourcePolicyConfiguration.ReadWrite.All` permissions for the setup requests.
+- An administrator with the [Privileged Role Administrator](~/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#privileged-role-administrator) role to [grant tenant-wide admin consent](~/identity/enterprise-apps/grant-admin-consent.md) for the read application's Microsoft Graph **application permissions**.
+- The read application's permission list, determined from the Microsoft Graph API reference for each read your policies make. The [live-read validation example](#validate-a-live-privileged-read) uses the `Application.Read.All` application permission.
+
+Activate any eligible roles through Privileged Identity Management (PIM) before starting. Graph Explorer's delegated setup permissions are separate from the privileged-read application's application permissions.
+
+## Configure the application
+
+Use the Microsoft Entra admin center to configure the application's API permissions and grant admin consent. Use Microsoft Graph Explorer for the Microsoft Graph setup requests below.
+
+### Add application permissions
+
+Use the application owner account for these steps.
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com/) with the application owner account listed in [Prerequisites](#prerequisites). Confirm you're working in the target tenant.
+1. Browse to **Entra ID** > **App registrations** > **Owned applications**, and select the existing privileged-read application.
+1. On the application's **Overview** page, record the following values:
+
+    | Value | Used for |
+    | --- | --- |
+    | **Application (client) ID** | Requesting the federated credential subject and setting the privileged-read app. |
+    | **Object ID** | Creating the federated identity credential on the application object. |
+    | **Directory (tenant) ID** | Setting the tenant-specific issuer for the federated identity credential. |
+
+    Copy **Object ID** from the app registration, not from **Enterprise applications**, which shows the service principal's object ID.
+
+1. Under **Manage**, select **API permissions** > **Add a permission**.
+1. Select **Microsoft Graph** > **Application permissions**. Don't select **Delegated permissions** for the privileged-read app.
+1. Search for and select only the read permissions required by your policies. For the [live-read validation example](#validate-a-live-privileged-read), select `Application.Read.All`.
+1. Select **Add permissions**.
+1. Review the **Configured permissions** list. Confirm the required Microsoft Graph permissions have **Application** as their **Type**. Don't add application-management or policy-management permissions to this app.
+
+### Grant admin consent
+
+Have the administrator with an active **Privileged Role Administrator** role complete these steps.
+
+1. Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center in the same tenant.
+1. Browse to **Entra ID** > **App registrations** > **All applications** and select the privileged-read app.
+1. Confirm its **Application (client) ID** matches the value recorded above.
+1. Open **API permissions** and review the full permission list.
+1. Select **Grant admin consent for \<tenant name\>**, then select **Yes** to confirm.
+1. Confirm the required application permissions show **Granted for \<tenant name\>** in the **Status** column.
+
+Continue with the following Graph Explorer procedures using the application owner account listed in [Prerequisites](#prerequisites). Don't create a client secret.
+
+### Create the federated identity credential
+
+1. In Graph Explorer, call [getFederatedIdentityCredentialSubject](/graph/api/resourcepolicyconfiguration-getfederatedidentitycredentialsubject?view=graph-rest-beta&preserve-view=true). Use the application's client ID:
+
+    ```http
+    GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/resourcePolicy/configuration/getFederatedIdentityCredentialSubject(appId='<application-client-id>')
+    ```
+
+1. Copy the response's `value` exactly. The subject is specific to the tenant and app; don't construct it or reuse another app's subject.
+1. [Create the credential](/graph/api/federatedidentitycredential-post) with the following request. Replace every placeholder, using the application object's ID in the path:
+
+    ```http
+    POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/applications/<application-object-id>/federatedIdentityCredentials
+    Content-Type: application/json
+
+    {
+      "name": "entra-resource-policy",
+      "issuer": "https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant-id>/v2.0",
+      "subject": "<value-returned-by-the-subject-function>",
+      "audiences": [
+        "api://AzureADTokenExchange"
+      ]
+    }
+    ```
+
+1. Confirm the response is `201 Created`.
+
+Match issuer, subject, and audience exactly, including case. Don't use `common`, `organizations`, or the v1 issuer, append a trailing slash to the issuer, or append `/.default` to the audience.
+
+### Set the privileged-read app
+
+1. Read the current configuration and copy `@odata.etag`, if present:
+
+    ```http
+    GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/resourcePolicy/configuration
+    ```
+
+1. Update the configured app ID with the application's client ID:
+
+    ```http
+    PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/resourcePolicy/configuration
+    Content-Type: application/json
+    If-Match: <current-configuration-etag>
+    ```
+
+    ```json
+    {
+      "privilegedReadSetting": {
+        "appId": "<application-client-id>"
+      }
+    }
+    ```
+
+1. Read the configuration again and confirm the intended app ID is saved.
+
+For initial configuration, omit `If-Match` because the empty configuration has no ETag. For later updates, use the latest ETag; after `412 Precondition Failed`, reread the configuration before retrying. See [Update resourcePolicyConfiguration](/graph/api/resourcepolicyconfiguration-update?view=graph-rest-beta&preserve-view=true).
+
+Configure the application before creating or updating a policy definition that uses `fetchAsPolicy()`.
+
+## Validate a live privileged read
+
+After configuring the app or changing its credentials or consent, use this test to read an application's ID through `fetchAsPolicy()`. Run it before deploying dependent policies. It doesn't create a definition or assignment or update the application.
+
+For this validation, you need:
+
+- A work or school account in the target tenant with an active [Resource Policy Administrator](resource-policy-concepts.md#roles-and-api-permissions) role.
+- The [Microsoft Graph PowerShell SDK](/powershell/microsoftgraph/installation), with admin consent for Microsoft Graph PowerShell's delegated `ResourcePolicyEvaluation.Read.All` and `ResourcePolicyDefinition.ReadWrite.All` permissions. A grant to Graph Explorer doesn't grant these permissions to Microsoft Graph PowerShell.
+- The configured privileged-read app with the consented `Application.Read.All` **application permission**, and an existing application's object ID in the same tenant. The evaluation client's permissions don't replace the app's permission.
+
+Activate an eligible role through Privileged Identity Management (PIM) before signing in. Run these steps in the same PowerShell session:
+
+1. Authenticate Microsoft Graph PowerShell. Replace `<tenant-id>` with your tenant ID:
+
+    ```powershell
+    Connect-MgGraph -TenantId '<tenant-id>' -Scopes `
+        'ResourcePolicyEvaluation.Read.All', 'ResourcePolicyDefinition.ReadWrite.All'
+    ```
+
+1. Prepare the validation request. Replace `<application-object-id>` with the application object's ID, not its client ID or service principal ID. The policy reports compliance only if the read returns HTTP `200` and the expected ID:
+
+    ```powershell
+    $applicationObjectId = '<application-object-id>'
+    $fetchPath = '/v1.0/applications/{0}?$select=id' -f $applicationObjectId
+    $policy = @"
+    package graph.privileged_read_validation["1.0.0"]
+
+    __metadata__ := {
+        "title": "Validate a privileged read",
+        "description": "Check access to the configured application.",
+        "selector": {
+            "resourceName": "microsoft.graph.application",
+            "operations": ["updateOrUpsert"]
+        }
+    }
+
+    default deny := {"result": true, "reasons": ["Privileged read validation failed."]}
+
+    deny := {"result": false, "reasons": []} if {
+        response := fetchAsPolicy({"relativePathUri": "$fetchPath"})
+        response.code == 200
+        response.data.id == "$applicationObjectId"
+    }
+    "@
+
+    $body = @{
+        policy = $policy
+        resourceUri = "/v1.0/applications/$applicationObjectId"
+        httpMethod = 'patch'
+        resourceBody = @{ displayName = 'Privileged read validation' }
+        enforcementMode = 'doNotEnforce'
+        isResultDetailed = $true
+    }
+    ```
+
+1. Submit the request to [evaluatePolicy](/graph/api/resourcepolicyroot-evaluatepolicy?view=graph-rest-beta&preserve-view=true). The request omits `fetchResponses` so that the service performs a real read, not a simulated response:
+
+    ```powershell
+    $result = Invoke-MgGraphRequest -Method POST `
+        -Uri 'https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/resourcePolicy/evaluatePolicy' `
+        -ContentType 'application/json' -Body ($body | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10)
+    $result | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 20
+    ```
+
+1. Confirm `appliedPoliciesEffects: "compliant"` and no loading or evaluation errors in `details`. A failed read, non-200 response, or mismatched ID isn't success. In `doNotEnforce` mode, `isBlocked: false` alone doesn't prove the read worked.
+
+Repeat the test for the specific reads your policies require. This example verifies application-read access, not every Microsoft Graph permission.
+
+Saving an app ID doesn't verify its read permissions. Use the live-read test after configuration or consent changes.
+
+## Maintain or disable privileged reads
+
+Use the following procedures to replace the application or stop privileged reads.
+
+### Replace the application
+
+1. Prepare the new app's federated credential and consent using [Configure the application](#configure-the-application).
+1. [Update the configured app ID](#set-the-privileged-read-app) with the current ETag, then rerun live-read validation.
+1. Review dependent policies and granted permissions. Revoke obsolete grants explicitly; adding a permission doesn't remove old grants.
+
+Federated credentials don't need scheduled secret rotation. If a credential changes unexpectedly, restore its exact trust values and retest.
+
+### Disable privileged reads
+
+> [!WARNING]
+> This change disables privileged reads tenant-wide and affects every policy that uses `fetchAsPolicy()`.
+
+1. Review all policies that use `fetchAsPolicy()` and how they handle failed reads.
+1. [Update the configuration](#set-the-privileged-read-app) with `appId` set to `null`:
+
+    ```json
+    {
+      "privilegedReadSetting": {
+        "appId": null
+      }
+    }
+    ```
+
+For configuration or read failures, see [Troubleshoot unexpected results](resource-policy-test-troubleshoot.md#troubleshoot-unexpected-results). Don't treat a failed read as evidence of compliance; test how your policies handle read errors.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Author resource policies with Rego](resource-policy-rego.md).
+- [Test and troubleshoot a resource policy](resource-policy-test-troubleshoot.md).
+- [Safely deploy resource policy assignments](resource-policy-safe-deployment.md).

+---
+title: "Quickstart: Assign and test a built-in Microsoft Entra resource policy (preview)"
+description: Assign a built-in resource policy in report-only mode and compare simulated compliant and noncompliant requests without creating applications.
+ms.topic: quickstart

+ai-usage: ai-generated
+# Customer intent: As a tenant administrator, I want to assign and test a built-in policy so that I can understand its decisions without writing Rego or creating applications.
+---
+
+# Quickstart: Assign and test a built-in Microsoft Entra resource policy (preview)
+
+Use the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com/) to assign a built-in resource policy in report-only mode and [Microsoft Graph Explorer](https://developer.microsoft.com/graph/graph-explorer) to test its decisions with simulated requests. You don't need to write a policy, create applications, or enable enforcement.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- An approved test environment.
+- A Microsoft Entra ID Governance service plan to create and activate the assignment, including report-only assignments. See [licensing requirements](licensing.md#resource-policy-preview).
+- One work or school account in the test tenant. Use this same account and tenant in the Microsoft Entra admin center and Microsoft Graph Explorer throughout the quickstart, including cleanup.
+
+### Microsoft Entra roles for your account
+
+Use an active [Resource Policy Administrator](resource-policy-concepts.md#roles-and-api-permissions) role to create and delete the assignment and evaluate assigned policies.
+
+If the role is eligible through Privileged Identity Management (PIM), activate it before starting.
+
+### Delegated permissions for Microsoft Graph Explorer
+
+Before starting, have an administrator grant consent in the test tenant for Microsoft Graph Explorer's **delegated** `ResourcePolicyEvaluation.Read.All` permission. This permission lets you run `evaluateAssignedPolicies` without performing the proposed write.
+
+Assignment creation and cleanup use the Microsoft Entra admin center, so you don't need to grant Graph Explorer assignment-management permissions.
+
+## 1. Select a built-in policy and assign it in your tenant
+
+Use the **Require a department prefix for application names** built-in policy. This policy requires application names to use an allowed department prefix and contain no banned words.
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) with the test-tenant account described in [Prerequisites](#prerequisites).
+1. Browse to **Tenant governance** > **Definitions**.
+1. On the **Built in** tab, find the **Require a department prefix for application names** policy definition and review the description.
+1. Select **Add assignment** on the chosen policy definition.
+1. On **Settings**, use assignment identifier `enforce_application_name_prefix` and policy version `1.0.0`. Set **Status** to **On** and **Enforcement** to **Report-only**. Leave other properties at their defaults.
+1. On **Parameters**, select **Edit allowed_departments** and enter the following case-sensitive prefixes, one value per row:
+
+    - `Engineering-`
+    - `Marketing-`
+    - `IT-`
+    - `HR-`
+    - `Finance-`
+    - `Sales-`
+
+    Use **Add row** for the additional `Sales-` value, then select **Apply**. Leave `banned_word_list` and `client_appid_exclusion_list` empty.
+1. On **Review**, review the summary and add the assignment.
+
+**On** enables evaluation; **Report-only** records results without blocking requests through this assignment.
+
+## 2. Validate without performing a write
+
+Use `evaluateAssignedPolicies` in Graph Explorer to compare names with and without an allowed prefix, without creating applications. The action evaluates all applicable assignments, so find `enforce_application_name_prefix` in `details` to identify this quickstart's results.
+
+The evaluation action reflects saved assignment settings without waiting for [changes to propagate to real requests](resource-policy-evaluation.md#assignment-propagation).
+
+Sign in to [Microsoft Graph Explorer](https://developer.microsoft.com/graph/graph-explorer) with the same account and tenant you used in the Microsoft Entra admin center. Confirm that Graph Explorer has the delegated permissions listed in [Prerequisites](#prerequisites).
+
+### Check a noncompliant application name
+
+Use `Inventory-Taker`, which doesn't start with any of the configured department prefixes.
+
+1. In [Microsoft Graph Explorer](https://developer.microsoft.com/graph/graph-explorer), select **POST** and **beta**.
+1. Enter the following request URL:
+
+    ```http
+    https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/resourcePolicy/evaluateAssignedPolicies
+    ```
+
+1. Select **Request Body** and enter the following JSON:
+
+    ```json
+    {
+      "resourceUri": "/beta/applications",
+      "httpMethod": "post",
+      "resourceBody": {
+        "displayName": "Inventory-Taker"
+      },
+      "scope": "/",
+      "isResultDetailed": true
+    }
+    ```
+
+1. Select **Run query**.
+1. In **Response preview**, inspect the evaluation result. Select **Expand** if you need more space.
+
+With this report-only assignment, expect **200 OK** and the following fields:
+
+| Field | Value |
+| --- | --- |
+| `appliedPoliciesEffects` | `deny` |
+| `isBlocked` | `false` |
+| `details[].assignmentUniqueName` | `enforce_application_name_prefix` |
+| `details[].assignedPolicyDisplayName` | Require a department prefix for application names |
+| `details[].appliedPolicyEffects` | `deny` |
+
+The matching entry in `details` includes this reason:
+
+> The application name needs an allowed department prefix. Add a prefix from allowed_departments, then try again.
+
+**200 OK** means the evaluation completed, not that the name is compliant. The `deny` effect identifies the violation; `isBlocked: false` reflects report-only mode. Other applicable assignments can affect the overall result.
+
+### Check a compliant application name
+
+Use `Sales-Inventory-Taker`, which starts with the configured `Sales-` prefix.
+
+1. Keep **POST**, **beta**, and the same evaluation request URL.
+1. In **Request Body**, change only `displayName` from `Inventory-Taker` to `Sales-Inventory-Taker`. Keep all other values unchanged.
+1. Select **Run query**.
+1. In **Response preview**, find the result for `enforce_application_name_prefix`.
+
+With this configuration, expect **200 OK** and the following fields:
+
+| Field | Value |
+| --- | --- |
+| `appliedPoliciesEffects` | `compliant` |
+| `isBlocked` | `false` |
+| `details[].assignmentUniqueName` | `enforce_application_name_prefix` |
+| `details[].appliedPolicyEffects` | `compliant` |
+
+The response message is:
+
+> Resource is compliant with assigned policies.
+
+Both examples return `isBlocked: false`. Compare the policy effects to distinguish compliance from a report-only violation.
+
+## 3. Clean up or continue
+
+To continue with the [tutorial](resource-policy-tutorial-portal.md), keep `enforce_application_name_prefix` **On** and **Report-only**, with its version and parameters unchanged. Skip deletion.
+
+If you're stopping here, delete the assignment. The simulated tests created no applications to clean up.
+
+1. Browse to **Tenant governance** > **Assignments**.
+1. Select the checkbox for `enforce_application_name_prefix`. Confirm that only the intended assignment is selected, including any selections hidden by the current filter.
+1. Select **Delete**.
+1. In **Remove assignment?**, confirm **Selected items: 1.**, then select **Delete**.
+
+Deleting the assignment stops it from applying the policy and moves it to **Deleted items**. You can restore it for 30 days.
+
+## Next steps
+
+Follow [Tutorial: Observe and enforce a built-in resource policy](resource-policy-tutorial-portal.md) to test real requests, inspect audit events, enable enforcement, and verify recovery.
+
+## Related content
+

+- [Create and manage resource policies in the Microsoft Entra admin center](resource-policy-manage-portal.md).
+- [Safely deploy resource policy assignments](resource-policy-safe-deployment.md).

+---
+title: Author Microsoft Entra resource policies with Rego (preview)
+description: Learn the Rego structure, normalized request input, applicability rules, parameters, and Microsoft Graph read functions used by resource policies.
+ms.topic: concept-article
+ms.date: 11/11/2026
+ai-usage: ai-generated
+# Customer intent: As a policy author, I want to understand the resource policy Rego contract so that I can create and test custom policies.
+---
+
+# Author Microsoft Entra resource policies with Rego (preview)
+
+Use Rego to author a custom Microsoft Entra resource policy when a built-in policy doesn't meet your requirements. Rego evaluates structured data against declarative rules. Resource policy uses those rules to identify noncompliant Microsoft Graph requests.
+
+You don't need to author Rego to [assign a built-in policy](resource-policy-quickstart-portal.md).
+
+## Required policy structure
+
+A custom policy contains these elements.
+
+| Element | Purpose |
+| --- | --- |
+| `package graph.<uniqueName>["X.Y.Z"]` | Identifies the policy and its semantic version. The name after `graph.` must match the definition's `uniqueName`. |
+| `__metadata__` | Defines descriptive metadata, the required selector, and any parameter schema. |
+| `__metadata__.selector` | Identifies the target resource type or action and applicable operations. |
+| `deny` | Reports whether the request is noncompliant. |
+
+An optional `applicable` rule can exclude requests that match the selector. Without it, matching requests continue to `deny` evaluation.
+
+Start a new custom definition at version `1.0.0`. Declare later versions in the package name when you update the definition. The version uses three nonnegative integers separated by periods.
+
+Choose a definition `uniqueName` that matches `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,127}`: an ASCII letter followed by up to 127 ASCII letters, digits, or underscores. The prefixes `microsoft` and `ms`, including `msft`, and the exact names `utils` and `input` are reserved regardless of case. For example, use `contosoApplicationNaming`.
+
+Use the same name in the Rego package, the JSON `uniqueName` property when supplied, URL keys, and an assignment's `assignedPolicy.policyUniqueName`. URL encoding doesn't make an invalid name valid.
+
+An assignment's own `uniqueName` is a separate identifier. It uses the same character and length rules and reserved prefixes, but the definition-specific reserved names `utils` and `input` don't apply to assignment names.
+
+The optional metadata `category` accepts `notSpecified`, `workloadIdentity`, `identityAndTenant`, `privilegedAccess`, `zeroTrust`, `agenticIdentity`, or `networkAccess`.
+
+Resource policy supports a restricted set of native Rego built-ins. Check [Disabled Rego built-in functions](resource-policy-service-limits.md#disabled-rego-built-in-functions) before using a function from the broader Rego language.
+
+For general language guidance, see the [Open Policy Agent policy language documentation](https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/policy-language).
+
+## Applicability metadata
+
+In `__metadata__.selector`, set `resourceName` to a [supported resource type or action](resource-policy-supported-resources.md). Set `operations` to a nonempty array of the operations that the policy evaluates. Use the exact casing shown for resource names and operations.
+
+| Operation | Use |
+| --- | --- |
+| `create` | Evaluate resource creation. |
+| `updateOrUpsert` | Evaluate resource updates or upserts. |
+| `delete` | Evaluate resource deletion. |
+| `invokeAction` | Evaluate an action invocation. |
+
+Specify operations explicitly so readers and reviewers can see the policy's intended coverage.
+
+For resource targets, `includeDerivedTypes` defaults to `true`. Set it to `false` to match only the named resource type. For action targets, specify the binding type and action name in `resourceName`, and omit `includeDerivedTypes`.
+
+## Example custom policy
+
+This custom policy requires new application display names to start with `Contoso-`. It isn't the quickstart's built-in naming policy.
+
+```rego
+package graph.application_name_prefix["1.0.0"]
+
+__metadata__ := {
+    "title": "Application name prefix",
+    "description": "Requires new application display names to start with Contoso-.",
+    "category": "workloadIdentity",
+    "selector": {
+        "resourceName": "microsoft.graph.application",
+        "operations": ["create"]
+    }
+}
+
+default deny := {"result": false, "reasons": []}
+
+deny := {
+    "result": true,
+    "reasons": ["Use an application display name that starts with Contoso-."]
+} if {
+    resource := object.get(input, "resource", {})
+    name := object.get(resource, "displayName", "")
+    not startswith(name, "Contoso-")
+}
+```
+
+The default result is compliant. The rule returns a noncompliant result and an actionable explanation when the prefix is missing.
+
+This policy targets creation only. An update payload can omit unchanged properties, so don't apply the same check to updates without accounting for partial request bodies and, when necessary, existing resource state.
+
+## Format policy source
+
+Keep each line within 1,024 characters. Longer lines return `line exceeds maximum column width of 1024`, even when the policy is within the [definition-size limit](resource-policy-service-limits.md#definitions-assignments-and-content).
+
+Split objects, arrays, and rule bodies across lines. For a long description, use a raw multiline string enclosed in backticks, as in this metadata fragment:
+
+```rego
+__metadata__ := {
+    "description": `Requires application display names to start with Contoso-.
+Evaluate this requirement when an application is created.`
+}
+```
+
+Line breaks and indentation inside the backticks are part of the description and count toward its 1,024-character limit. Reformatting doesn't increase the metadata or total policy-size limits.
+
+## Submit and retrieve policy source
+
+Definition create and update requests accept `Content-Type: text/plain`. Send the complete Rego policy as the request body, including the versioned package declaration and metadata. On creation, the service derives the definition's name from that package.
+
+Alternatively, send JSON with the source in `rule.policy`. In either format, Rego supplies the definition's version, display name, description, category, parameter schema, and selector.
+
+To retrieve custom policy source, use `Accept: text/plain` when reading a current definition, a soft-deleted definition, or an individual previous version. Use the JSON representation when you need the surrounding definition metadata. ETags and update preconditions still apply.
+
+## Deny results and enforcement
+
+The `deny` rule can return a Boolean or an object with a Boolean `result` and a `reasons` array.
+
+- A false result identifies a compliant request.
+- A true result identifies a noncompliant request.
+
+The rule doesn't determine whether the request is blocked. The assignment's `enforcementMode` controls that behavior. See [How resource policy evaluation works](resource-policy-evaluation.md).
+
+Write reasons that explain how to correct the request. Don't include sensitive resource data or credentials in reason text.
+
+## Normalized request input
+
+The service normalizes the request into an `input` object before evaluation.
+
+| Input element | Contents |
+| --- | --- |
+| `input.request.apiVersion` | The Microsoft Graph version of the evaluated request. |
+| `input.request.authContext` | Selected authentication context, including the caller application, tenant, and available subject information. |
+| `input.request.authContext.isAgenticSession` | Present with the value `true` for an agentic session. Its absence doesn't represent an explicit `false` value. |
+| `input.request.uriSegments` | URI segments with resource types and keys when present. |
+| `input.request.resourceKeys` | Keys of the target resource, when the request identifies an existing resource. |
+| `input.resource` | The normalized request body, when the request has a body. |
+
+For example, a normalized request body for application creation can include:
+
+```json
+{
+  "resource": {
+    "displayName": "Contoso-Inventory",
+    "signInAudience": "AzureADMyOrg"
+  }
+}
+```
+
+This fragment illustrates `input.resource`; it isn't a complete normalized input document.
+
+Properties can be absent. For example, the request might not have a body or a target resource key. Don't treat an absent property as proof of a particular identity type. `input.request.authContext.isAppOnly` is a Boolean.
+
+Use the evaluation action's `includeNormalizedRequestInput` option to inspect the service-generated input. See [Test and troubleshoot a resource policy](resource-policy-test-troubleshoot.md).
+
+## Parameters and defaults
+
+Define typed parameters in `__metadata__.paramsSchema`. Supply assignment-specific values through the assignment's JSON `params` property.
+
+Read values through `data.graph.<definitionUniqueName>["<version>"].params`, matching the package name and version. An import alias lets you use `params.<name>`:
+
+```rego
+package graph.application_name_prefix_parameterized["1.0.0"]
+
+import data.graph.application_name_prefix_parameterized["1.0.0"].params as params
+```
+
+For example, use `params.required_prefix` after this import. Update the import when you change the package version, and don't declare your own `params` rule.
+
+Rego `default` declarations must use constant expressions. Don't put references to `input`, other rules, or function calls in a default declaration.
+
+For schema and assignment-value examples, see [Resource policy parameters](resource-policy-parameters.md).
+
+## Read additional Microsoft Graph data
+
+Some requirements need information that isn't in the request body. Use `fetchAsPolicy()` for additional read-only Microsoft Graph requests. It uses a configured, customer-owned privileged-read application independently of the request caller's permissions.
+
+Configure the [privileged-read application](resource-policy-privileged-read-app.md) before creating or updating a definition that uses this function.
+
+The function takes a request object containing `relativePathUri`, including the Microsoft Graph API version. The result contains an HTTP response `code` and response `data`.
+
+The following fragment checks that an existing application's display name starts with `Contoso-` after an update. Use it as the `deny` logic for an application policy whose selector sets `operations` to `["updateOrUpsert"]`. It uses the proposed name when the update supplies `displayName`, or the existing name from the read response when the update omits it:
+
+```rego
+default deny := true
+
+deny := false if {
+    response := fetchAsPolicy({
+        "relativePathUri": sprintf(
+            "/%s/applications/%s?$select=displayName",
+            [input.request.apiVersion, input.request.resourceKeys.id]
+        )
+    })
+    response.code == 200
+    name_after_update := object.get(
+        object.get(input, "resource", {}),
+        "displayName",
+        response.data.displayName
+    )
+    is_string(name_after_update)
+    startswith(name_after_update, "Contoso-")
+}
+```
+
+Use this pattern only when normalized input contains the required resource key. The example reports noncompliance if the read fails, required data is missing, or the name check fails. The assignment's enforcement mode determines whether that result blocks the request.
+
+Additional reads increase latency and consume Microsoft Graph request capacity. Request only the properties you need, prefer a specific resource to a collection, and don't rely on paging. Keep calls within the [additional-read limits](resource-policy-service-limits.md#additional-read-limits).
+
+## Test before assignment
+
+Build tests for compliant, noncompliant, missing-property, and excluded requests. Validate applicability separately from the `deny` result.
+
+Use service evaluation before deployment. A locally valid policy isn't evidence that the service accepts it or that its assignments behave as intended.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Test and troubleshoot a resource policy](resource-policy-test-troubleshoot.md).
+- [Resource policy parameters](resource-policy-parameters.md).
+- [Update and retire resource policies](resource-policy-lifecycle.md).

Use this account in the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) to manage assignments and in Microsoft Graph Explorer to test policies and read evaluation audit events.
+- [Microsoft Graph Explorer](https://developer.microsoft.com/graph/graph-explorer) with admin consent for the delegated `ResourcePolicyEvaluation.Read.All` and `AuditLog.Read.All` permissions.
+- For real `fetchAsPolicy()` reads during `evaluatePolicy`, a [configured privileged-read app](resource-policy-privileged-read-app.md) and admin consent for the delegated `ResourcePolicyDefinition.ReadWrite.All` permission in Graph Explorer.
+- An approved test plan for the target tenant.
+- A policy owner, contacts for affected application owners, and saved settings for recovery.
+
+Activate any eligible roles through Privileged Identity Management (PIM) before starting. Graph Explorer doesn't need assignment-management permissions for this workflow because assignment changes use the Microsoft Entra admin center.
+
+## 1. Define the intended impact
+
+1. Select the policy version and parameter values. Record the resource changes it should allow and block.
+1. Identify existing business-critical applications that might need temporary exceptions, and contact their owners.
+
+## 2. Test representative requests
+
+1. Use `evaluatePolicy` with supplied Rego, parameter values, and a proposed request URI, HTTP method, and body. Use `evaluateAssignedPolicies` for existing assignments. See [Test and troubleshoot a resource policy](resource-policy-test-troubleshoot.md).
+1. Test requests that should pass, requests that should fail, and requests covered by an intended exception. Include missing values or partial updates where relevant.
+1. Inspect the policy results and errors, not just the HTTP status. Check that each result matches your expectation.
+
+Evaluation actions don't perform the simulated write, but policies can still make real additional reads.
+
+## 3. Assign without enforcement
+
+1. [Create an assignment](resource-policy-manage-portal.md#create-an-assignment) with **Status** set to **On** and **Enforcement** set to **Report-only** (`doNotEnforce`). Check the policy version and parameters.
+1. Wait for [assignment changes to take effect](resource-policy-evaluation.md#assignment-propagation).
+
+For a version update, create this assignment for the new version and leave the old assignment enforced. Follow [Roll out the new version](resource-policy-lifecycle.md#roll-out-the-new-version) for the handover.
+
+## 4. Review impact
+
+1. Choose an observation period that covers normal business operations, including infrequent automation.
+1. [Retrieve evaluation audit events](resource-policy-logs.md#assess-assignment-impact-from-evaluation-events) and find the intended assignment and version in the policy details.
+1. List affected applications, violations, and evaluation errors. Review errors separately, and check whether approved exceptions work as intended.
+
+A quiet period or missing events doesn't prove readiness for enforcement.
+
+## 5. Resolve violations and review exceptions
+
+You don't have to update every existing application before enforcing a policy. When the policy supports application exceptions, use an approved exception list to keep business-critical applications running. Other applications, including new ones, must meet the policy's requirements.
+
+1. With application owners, decide which applications can be updated now and which need temporary exceptions.
+1. Add approved applications to the supported exception parameter, using the identifiers specified by its description.
+1. For each exception, record an owner, required application changes, a target completion date, and removal criteria. Include unresolved evaluation errors in the investigation plan.
+1. Retest allowed, denied, and excepted requests with the updated values. After assignment changes take effect, confirm the results in evaluation audit events.
+
+Track remediation after enforcement. Once an application makes compliant changes, remove its exception, wait for the change to take effect, and verify its normal requests still succeed. See [Parameter update behavior](resource-policy-parameters.md#assignment-update-behavior).
+
+## 6. Enable enforcement
+
+1. Get the policy owner's approval of the results, temporary exceptions and remediation plans, and recovery settings.
+1. [Edit the assignment](resource-policy-manage-portal.md#edit-an-existing-assignment) to set **Enforcement** to **Enforce** (`enforce`).
+1. Wait for [assignment changes to take effect](resource-policy-evaluation.md#assignment-propagation). For a version update, confirm new enforcement before disabling the old assignment.
+1. Verify a compliant request succeeds, a noncompliant request outside the exception list is blocked by this policy, and an excepted workflow still works.
+
+Continue reviewing evaluation audit events and the exception-removal plan. Other policies and service controls can still affect the same requests.
+
+## 7. Recover from unexpected impact
+
+Choose the recovery path for your deployment.
+
+### First deployment
+
+Use this recovery path when you don't have a previous enforced version or working parameter values to restore.
+
+Turning off the assignment or returning it to report-only removes its enforcement protection; neither change takes effect on every request immediately.
+
+1. [Turn off the affected assignment](resource-policy-manage-portal.md#turn-off-an-assignment) to stop evaluation. To keep evaluating without blocking, [edit it](resource-policy-manage-portal.md#edit-an-existing-assignment) instead: keep **Status** set to **On** and set **Enforcement** to **Report-only**.
+1. Wait for [assignment changes to take effect](resource-policy-evaluation.md#assignment-propagation), then retest the affected workflow. Other enforced assignments and service controls can still block requests.
+1. Correct and test the policy or parameters. Repeat the report-only assessment and approval steps before enabling enforcement again.
+
+### Version or parameter changes
+
+For a version regression, re-enable the retained old assignment and confirm it is enforcing before disabling the new one. Follow [Roll back to the previous version](resource-policy-lifecycle.md#roll-back-to-the-previous-version).
+
+For an incorrect parameter change, restore the saved working values, allow the change to take effect, and retest the affected requests. Review any temporary application exceptions with their owners while you investigate.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Quickstart: Assign a built-in resource policy](resource-policy-quickstart-portal.md).
+- [Create and manage resource policies in the Microsoft Entra admin center](resource-policy-manage-portal.md).
+- [Analyze resource policy evaluation audit logs](resource-policy-logs.md).

+---
+title: Microsoft Entra resource policy service limits (preview)
+description: Review limits for resource policy definitions, assignments, Rego built-ins, request evaluation, additional reads, version history, and API requests.
+ms.topic: reference
+ms.date: 11/11/2026
+ai-usage: ai-generated
+# Customer intent: As a policy administrator, I want to understand service limits so that I can plan policy assignments and keep evaluation within supported capacity.
+---
+
+# Microsoft Entra resource policy service limits (preview)
+
+Resource policy limits apply to policy objects, policy content, request evaluation, and API request rates. Keep your policies and additional Microsoft Graph reads within the limits below.
+
+## Definitions, assignments, and content
+
+| Scope | Limit | Value | Details |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Resource type | Custom definition versions | 25. | Includes current and previous versions. Built-in definitions don't count. Creating or restoring a version that would exceed the limit returns HTTP 400. |
+| Tenant | Custom definition versions | 1,000. | Soft-deleted versions don't count, but restoring them checks the quotas again. The definition collection's `$count` counts definitions, not individual versions. Exceeding the limit returns HTTP 400. |
+| Resource type | Policy assignments | 25. | Includes assignments to built-in and custom policies, even when disabled. Exceeding the limit returns HTTP 400. |
+| Tenant | Policy assignments | 1,000. | Includes disabled assignments and assignments to built-in policies. Soft-deleted assignments don't count, but restoring them checks the quotas again. Exceeding the limit returns HTTP 400. |
+| Definition version | Live assignments per tenant | 1. | Disabling an assignment doesn't allow a second assignment. Update the existing assignment to change its settings. |
+| Policy definition | Top-level Rego entries | 50. | Includes metadata and helper rule results. Policy validation returns HTTP 400 if exceeded. |
+| Policy definition | Rego source size in UTF-8 | 1 MiB (1,048,576 bytes). | Oversized source returns HTTP 413. For line-formatting requirements, see [Format policy source](resource-policy-rego.md#format-policy-source). |
+| Policy assignment | Serialized parameter values | 40 KiB (40,960 bytes). | Measured as compact UTF-8 JSON. Both submitted values and values after merging and applying defaults must fit. Exceeding the limit returns HTTP 413. |
+| Policy assignment | Serialized assignment size | 50 KiB (51,200 bytes). | Measured as compact UTF-8 JSON. Applies to the complete assignment after an update, not just changed properties. Exceeding the limit returns HTTP 413. |
+| Policy assignment evaluation | Distinct additional Microsoft Graph read paths | 2. | Covers both `applicable` and `deny` evaluations for one request. A different resource ID or query string counts as another path. See [Additional read limits](#additional-read-limits). |
+| Policy assignment evaluation | `fetchAsPolicy()` invocations, including repeated paths | 5. | Every call counts, even when it reads the same path again. The count resets for each incoming request. |
+| Request evaluation | Distinct additional-read paths across assignments | 10. | Shared across all assignments for one request. Reading the same path in multiple assignments counts once toward this limit. |
+| Additional Microsoft Graph read | `relativePathUri` length | 2,048 characters. | Includes the API version, resource path, and query string. |
+| Additional Microsoft Graph read | Response size | 100 KiB (102,400 bytes), by default. | Includes both `code` and `data` for live and simulated reads. Use `$select` to request only the properties your policy needs. |
+
+## Disabled Rego built-in functions
+
+Resource policy restricts the supported native Rego built-in functions. Only the functions listed here are permitted; all other native built-ins are disabled. For example, `time.now_ns` isn't permitted, including in metadata or helper rules.
+
+| Category | Permitted native built-ins |
+| --- | --- |
+| Aggregates | `count`, `max`, `min`, `sort`, `sum` |
+| Arrays | `array.concat`, `array.reverse`, `array.slice` |
+| Sets | `intersection`, `union` |
+| Numbers | `abs`, `ceil`, `floor`, `round`, `to_number` |
+| Type checks | `is_array`, `is_boolean`, `is_null`, `is_number`, `is_object`, `is_set`, `is_string` |
+| Bitwise operations | `bits.and`, `bits.lsh`, `bits.negate`, `bits.or`, `bits.rsh`, `bits.xor` |
+| Strings | `concat`, `contains`, `endswith`, `indexof`, `lower`, `replace`, `split`, `sprintf`, `startswith`, `strings.reverse`, `substring`, `trim`, `trim_left`, `trim_prefix`, `trim_right`, `trim_space`, `trim_suffix`, `upper` |
+| Objects | `object.filter`, `object.get`, `object.keys`, `object.remove`, `object.union` |
+| URL encoding and UUID parsing | `urlquery.encode`, `urlquery.decode`, `uuid.parse` |
+
+Use the exact names and casing shown.
+
+Calls to disallowed native built-ins cause policy validation or loading errors, not a policy-compliance result. Replace those calls with permitted functions and [test the policy](resource-policy-test-troubleshoot.md) before assigning it.
+
+Service-provided functions such as `fetchAsPolicy()` aren't native Rego built-ins. Their separate restrictions are described in [Additional read limits](#additional-read-limits).
+
+## Additional read limits
+
+Each assignment can read two distinct `relativePathUri` values per incoming request, across its `applicable` and `deny` rules. A different API version, resource ID, or query string, including `$select`, counts as another path.
+
+For example, reading `/v1.0/applications/<id>?$select=displayName` twice uses one distinct path but two invocations. Adding a read of another application uses the second path. A third distinct path causes that assignment's evaluation to fail. The limit counts requested URIs, not the number of objects returned by a collection read.
+
+Across assignments, the same path counts once toward the request-wide limit of 10 paths. Each assignment still counts every invocation, including repeated paths, toward its five-call limit.
+
+For an example that processes a read response, see [Read additional Microsoft Graph data](resource-policy-rego.md#read-additional-microsoft-graph-data).
+
+## Version history and deleted items
+
+A custom definition can have up to 10 previous versions, in addition to its current version. An update that would exceed this limit returns HTTP 400. Delete an unused previous version before publishing another update when the history limit is reached.
+
+Soft-deleted definitions and assignments are retained for 30 days.
+
+Individual previous-version deletion is permanent and doesn't use the soft-delete retention period.
+
+For dependency handling, see [Update and retire resource policies](resource-policy-lifecycle.md).
+
+## API request throttling
+
+These limits apply to management and explicit evaluation requests under `/admin/resourcePolicy`, separately for each app and tenant combination.
+
+| Request type | Preview limit per app per tenant | Equivalent sustained request rate |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Write policy definitions and assignments, or update configuration | 40 requests per 20 seconds | 2 requests per second |
+| Read policy definitions, assignments, and configuration | 60 requests per 20 seconds | 3 requests per second |
+| [evaluatePolicy](/graph/api/resourcepolicyroot-evaluatepolicy?view=graph-rest-beta&preserve-view=true) | 100 requests per 20 seconds | 5 requests per second |
+| [evaluateAssignedPolicies](/graph/api/resourcepolicyroot-evaluateassignedpolicies?view=graph-rest-beta&preserve-view=true) | 60 requests per 20 seconds | 3 requests per second |
+
+Automatic policy evaluation on ordinary Microsoft Graph write requests doesn't count toward these limits.
+
+Throttled requests return HTTP 429. Wait for the interval in the `Retry-After` header before retrying. For more information, see [Microsoft Graph throttling guidance](/graph/throttling).
+
+## Evaluation limits
+
+| Scope | Limit | Value |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Request being evaluated | Real or simulated request body size | 2 MiB (2,097,152 bytes), by default. |
+| `evaluatePolicy` | Simulated additional-read responses | 2. |
+| `evaluatePolicy` | Combined serialized `data` values in simulated responses | 2 MiB (2,097,152 bytes). |
+
+Keep request bodies within the size limit so your policies can evaluate them. For explicit evaluation actions, this limit applies to `resourceBody`, not the complete action payload.
+
+If the body is too large, policy evaluation is skipped and enforced policies can still block the request. An explicit evaluation can still return HTTP 200, so check the response message, `isBlocked`, and policy error details.
+
+Invalid simulated-response counts or oversized combined `data` values return HTTP 400. Correct the supplied responses and try again. Each simulated response must also fit within the [additional-read response limit](#additional-read-limits).
+
+Use [evaluation audit logs](resource-policy-logs.md) to investigate errors on real requests.
+

+
+- [Supported resources and actions](resource-policy-supported-resources.md).
+- [Author resource policies with Rego](resource-policy-rego.md).
+- [Resource policy known issues](resource-policy-known-issues.md).

+
+# Test and troubleshoot a Microsoft Entra resource policy (preview)
+
+Test custom Rego or assigned policies with simulated requests, then investigate unexpected results. Evaluation actions don't perform the requested resource change.
+
+## Choose your task
+
+| Task | Start here |
+| --- | --- |
+| Test custom policy logic in isolation. | [Evaluate custom policy logic](#evaluate-custom-policy-logic). |
+| Test or reproduce a decision from assigned policies. | [Evaluate assigned policies](#evaluate-assigned-policies). |
+| Check the configured application's live read access. | [Validate a live privileged read](resource-policy-privileged-read-app.md#validate-a-live-privileged-read). |

+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- A work or school account in the target tenant with an active [Resource Policy Evaluator](resource-policy-concepts.md#roles-and-api-permissions) or [Resource Policy Administrator](resource-policy-concepts.md#roles-and-api-permissions) role. Activate an eligible role through Privileged Identity Management (PIM) before signing in.
+- [Microsoft Graph Explorer](https://developer.microsoft.com/graph/graph-explorer), signed in to that tenant with this account, with admin consent for the delegated `ResourcePolicyEvaluation.Read.All` permission for the HTTP examples.
+
+These requirements cover simulated requests. Additional requirements for real reads and resource operations are listed with those procedures. Evaluation permissions don't grant policy management or target-resource write access.
+
+## Build a test matrix
+
+1. Prepare requests that should pass and fail. Record the URI, method, body, parameters, and expected applicability and compliance.
+1. Include relevant missing, null, empty, and boundary values, partial updates, excluded requests, and additional-read success and failure cases.
+1. Save the inputs, expected and actual results, and errors. Rerun these cases after changing policy logic or parameters.
+
+## Evaluate custom policy logic
+
+1. Prepare the Rego and test input. Replace the placeholders below, and add JSON `params` if needed. For parameterized Rego, check the [qualified reference or import alias](resource-policy-rego.md#parameters-and-defaults).
+1. In Graph Explorer, select **POST** and **beta**, and submit the following URL and JSON body to `evaluatePolicy`:
+
+    ```http
+    POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/resourcePolicy/evaluatePolicy
+    Content-Type: application/json
+    ```
+
+    ```json
+    {
+      "policy": "<complete Rego policy serialized as a JSON string>",
+      "resourceUri": "/v1.0/applications",
+      "httpMethod": "post",
+      "resourceBody": {
+        "displayName": "Contoso-Inventory",
+        "signInAudience": "AzureADMyOrg"
+      },
+      "enforcementMode": "doNotEnforce",
+      "isResultDetailed": true,
+      "includeNormalizedRequestInput": true
+    }
+    ```
+
+1. Select **Run query**.
+1. In **Response preview**, [compare the policy results and errors](#interpret-evaluation-results) with your expectations. Use normalized request input to investigate unexpected outcomes.
+
+This action doesn't create a definition or assignment.
+
+## Evaluate assigned policies
+
+1. Prepare the proposed request input without an inline `policy` property.
+1. In Graph Explorer, select **POST** and **beta**, and submit it to `evaluateAssignedPolicies`:
+
+    ```http
+    POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/resourcePolicy/evaluateAssignedPolicies
+    Content-Type: application/json
+    ```
+
+    ```json
+    {
+      "resourceUri": "/v1.0/applications",
+      "httpMethod": "post",
+      "resourceBody": {
+        "displayName": "Inventory",
+        "signInAudience": "AzureADMyOrg"
+      },
+      "scope": "/",
+      "isResultDetailed": true,
+      "includeNormalizedRequestInput": true
+    }
+    ```
+
+1. Select **Run query**.
+1. In **Response preview**, [inspect each assignment's results and errors](#interpret-evaluation-results), version, and parameters. Check whether another assignment affects the overall result.
+
+An evaluation action doesn't prove that a recent assignment change has reached request-time evaluation.
+
+## Interpret evaluation results
+
+Use these fields for both evaluation actions:
+
+| Field | Use |
+| --- | --- |
+| `appliedPoliciesEffects` | Check the combined effect, `deny` or `compliant`, alongside errors. |
+| `isBlocked` | Check whether the proposed request would be blocked under the enforcement settings and error behavior. |
+| `details` | Review policy outcomes, violation `reasons`, and errors. Request `isResultDetailed: true` to include these details. |
+
+For `evaluatePolicy`, a violation returns `appliedPoliciesEffects: "deny"` in both modes: `isBlocked` is `true` with `enforce` and `false` with `doNotEnforce`. Omitting the mode uses `doNotEnforce`.
+
+Inspect errors and skipped evaluations too. A payload-size error can block without a completed compliance evaluation.
+
+## Test additional reads with simulated responses
+
+1. Add `fetchResponses` to the `evaluatePolicy` request to test read handling without real additional reads. Supply a response for every read path the policy executes, matching `relativePathUri` and its query string exactly:
+
+    ```json
+    {
+      "fetchResponses": [
+        {
+          "relativePathUri": "/v1.0/applications/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001?$select=id,displayName",
+          "code": 200,
+          "data": {
+            "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001",
+            "displayName": "Contoso-Inventory"
+          }
+        }
+      ]
+    }
+    ```
+
+1. Run the tests with successful and failed read responses. An unmatched read produces an error, not a real request; an empty array permits no additional reads. Read URI validation still applies.
+1. Before deployment, meet the requirements in [Validate a live privileged read](#validate-a-live-privileged-read), then omit `fetchResponses` or set it to `null` to test real reads.
+
+Simulated responses need only evaluation permissions, but don't prove the configured app can read the resource.
+
+### Validate a live privileged read
+
+For real `fetchAsPolicy()` reads during `evaluatePolicy` in Graph Explorer, use an active [Resource Policy Administrator](resource-policy-concepts.md#roles-and-api-permissions) role and obtain admin consent for the additional delegated `ResourcePolicyDefinition.ReadWrite.All` permission. A [configured privileged-read app](resource-policy-privileged-read-app.md) supplies the application permissions for the reads your policy makes.
+
+Use the [live-read PowerShell walkthrough](resource-policy-privileged-read-app.md#validate-a-live-privileged-read) to verify application-read access after configuration or consent changes. Its PowerShell permissions are separate from Graph Explorer's grants.
+
+## Verify real request behavior
+
+For the operation you test, grant Graph Explorer the delegated permissions and use the user authorization specified by its Microsoft Graph API reference. For application creation, use the [tutorial prerequisites](resource-policy-tutorial-portal.md#prerequisites). If you need to create or change an assignment, also meet the [portal management prerequisites](resource-policy-manage-portal.md#prerequisites).
+
+To query evaluation audit events, use an active [Reports Reader](~/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#reports-reader) role and obtain admin consent for Graph Explorer's delegated `AuditLog.Read.All` permission.
+
+After the request-input tests pass:
+
+1. Use an enabled report-only assignment. For a version update, keep existing enforcement and use a [separate assignment for the new version](resource-policy-lifecycle.md#roll-out-the-new-version).
+1. Wait for [assignment propagation](resource-policy-evaluation.md#assignment-propagation).
+1. Perform an approved test operation with a caller that has the target-resource permissions.
+1. [Retrieve its evaluation event](resource-policy-logs.md#retrieve-evaluation-audit-events) by request ID. Check the intended assignment and version, and separate violations from errors.
+
+A real operation can create or modify resources. Use an approved test environment, and follow [safe deployment](resource-policy-safe-deployment.md) for enforcement and recovery.
+
+## Troubleshoot unexpected results
+
+| Symptom | Checks |
+| --- | --- |
+| The policy isn't evaluated. | Check assignment enablement, scope, resource type, operation, and policy applicability. |
+| A noncompliant request isn't blocked. | Check enforcement mode, propagation, and whether the result came from an evaluation action or an actual resource request. |
+| A request is blocked despite a `doNotEnforce` assignment. | Inspect other enforced assignments and other Microsoft Graph controls. |
+| A rule reports compliance unexpectedly. | Inspect normalized input, missing properties, parameter values, and the assigned policy version. Check that the [parameter reference or import](resource-policy-rego.md#parameters-and-defaults) matches the definition name and version. |
+| An assignment update is rejected. | Check the current ETag, the referenced version's parameter schema, and whether that version already has a live assignment, including a disabled assignment. Include `params` when changing the assigned version. |
+| No privileged-read app is configured. | [Configure the application](resource-policy-privileged-read-app.md) before testing real `fetchAsPolicy()` reads. |
+| The privileged-read configuration update fails validation. | Confirm tenant ownership, single-tenant registration, and exact federated credential values. See [Create the federated identity credential](resource-policy-privileged-read-app.md#create-the-federated-identity-credential). |
+| An additional read fails after successful configuration. | Check whether the app, service principal, consent, or federated credential changed. [Validate a live privileged read](resource-policy-privileged-read-app.md#validate-a-live-privileged-read), including the evaluation client's permission and role requirements. |
+| Only some additional reads fail. | Check the least-privileged permission and consent required for each failing API. |
+| An evaluation action succeeds but the resource operation fails. | Check the real caller's permissions, resource validation, propagation, and request differences. |
+
+## Inspect Rego logic locally
+
+You can use an approved local Rego evaluator to investigate individual rules with sanitized normalized input. Validate an optional `applicable` rule separately from `deny`.
+
+Don't upload tenant data, policy source, or authentication context to an external playground without authorization. Local tests don't verify service-specific functions, permissions, or enforcement. Rerun service tests after every policy change.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Author resource policies with Rego](resource-policy-rego.md).
+- [Configure a privileged-read app](resource-policy-privileged-read-app.md).
+- [Resource policy known issues](resource-policy-known-issues.md).
+- [Safely deploy resource policy assignments](resource-policy-safe-deployment.md).

+---
+title: "Tutorial: Observe and enforce a built-in Microsoft Entra resource policy (preview)"
+description: Continue from the resource policy quickstart to observe real requests, inspect audit events, enforce a policy, verify recovery, and clean up.
+ms.topic: tutorial
+ms.date: 11/12/2026
+ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-1030
+ai-usage: ai-generated
+# Customer intent: As a tenant administrator, I want to observe, enforce, and recover a built-in policy so that I can understand its complete lifecycle before planning a production rollout.
+---
+
+# Tutorial: Observe and enforce a built-in Microsoft Entra resource policy (preview)
+
+Continue from [Quickstart: Assign and test a built-in resource policy](resource-policy-quickstart-portal.md) to see how the same assignment affects real Microsoft Graph requests. Use the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com/) to manage the assignment and [Microsoft Graph Explorer](https://developer.microsoft.com/graph/graph-explorer) to create test applications and investigate evaluation audit events.
+
+In this tutorial, you:
+
+- Compare compliant and noncompliant requests in report-only mode.
+- Inspect the corresponding evaluation audit events.
+- Enable enforcement and verify allowed and blocked requests.
+- Return to report-only mode and verify recovery.
+- Remove the assignment and test applications.
+
+Unlike the quickstart's simulated evaluations, these tests create real application registrations when requests are allowed. Enforcement affects matching requests throughout the test tenant. Allow time between stages for assignment propagation and audit-event availability.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- Complete the [built-in policy quickstart](resource-policy-quickstart-portal.md). Retain its assignment, version, and parameter values. If you already deleted the assignment, follow the recovery instructions in [Confirm the starting assignment](#1-confirm-the-starting-assignment).
+- Keep the quickstart's Microsoft Entra ID Governance service plan to update or restore the assignment. See [licensing requirements](licensing.md#resource-policy-preview).
+- Use the same work or school account and test tenant in the Microsoft Entra admin center and Microsoft Graph Explorer throughout the tutorial, including cleanup.
+
+### Microsoft Entra roles for your account
+
+| Role | Purpose in this tutorial |
+| --- | --- |
+| [Resource Policy Administrator](resource-policy-concepts.md#roles-and-api-permissions) | Update, restore, and delete the assignment, and repeat simulated validation if needed. |
+| [Application Developer](~/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#application-developer) | Create the test app registrations and manage the apps you own, including deleting them during cleanup. |
+| [Reports Reader](~/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#reports-reader) | Read the evaluation audit-log events. |
+
+Application Developer lets you create test apps even when **Users can register applications** is **No**. You don't need it if default user permissions already let you create and manage your own apps.
+
+If a required role is eligible through Privileged Identity Management (PIM), activate it before starting.
+
+### Delegated permissions for Microsoft Graph Explorer
+
+Before starting, have an administrator grant consent in the test tenant for the following **delegated** Microsoft Graph permissions for **Microsoft Graph Explorer**:
+
+| Permission | Purpose in this tutorial |
+| --- | --- |
+| `AuditLog.Read.All` | Query evaluation audit events through `/auditLogs/resourcePolicy`. |
+| `Application.ReadWrite.All` | Create the test app registrations through `/applications`. |
+| `ResourcePolicyEvaluation.Read.All` | Retain the quickstart's grant to repeat simulated validation if you restore or change the assignment. |
+
+Grant these permissions to Graph Explorer, not the test apps. Assignment changes and app cleanup use the Microsoft Entra admin center with your account's roles and app ownership.
+
+## 1. Confirm the starting assignment
+
+1. Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center with the same account and tenant used in the quickstart.
+1. Browse to **Tenant governance** > **Assignments** and open `enforce_application_name_prefix`.
+1. Confirm the saved assignment settings:
+
+    | Setting | Expected value |
+    | --- | --- |
+    | Policy definition | Require a department prefix for application names |
+    | Policy version | `1.0.0` |
+    | Status | **On** |
+    | Enforcement | **Report-only** |
+    | `allowed_departments` | `Engineering-`, `Marketing-`, `IT-`, `HR-`, `Finance-`, `Sales-` |
+    | `banned_word_list` | Empty |
+    | `client_appid_exclusion_list` | Empty |
+
+1. Sign in to Graph Explorer with the same account and tenant. Confirm it has the delegated permissions listed in [Prerequisites](#prerequisites).
+
+If the assignment isn't ready, use the matching recovery path:
+
+| Assignment state | Action |
+| --- | --- |
+| Deleted | Find it under **Tenant governance** > **Deleted items** > **Assignments**. Verify its identity and saved **On / Report-only** settings before [restoring it](resource-policy-manage-portal.md#restore-deleted-items). |
+| Settings differ from the table above | [Edit the assignment](resource-policy-manage-portal.md#edit-an-existing-assignment) to restore those values. |
+| Neither live nor restorable | Repeat the quickstart. Don't create a second live assignment for the same policy version. |
+
+After restoring or correcting the assignment, repeat the quickstart's [simulated validation](resource-policy-quickstart-portal.md#2-validate-without-performing-a-write) before continuing.
+
+## 2. Review real request impact
+
+Wait for [assignment changes to propagate](resource-policy-evaluation.md#assignment-propagation), then test both names. This report-only assignment allows both requests, but other policies or service controls can still block them.
+
+1. In Graph Explorer, select **POST** and **beta**, and enter this request URL:
+
+    ```http
+    https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/applications
+    ```
+
+1. In **Request Body**, enter the noncompliant application name:
+
+    ```json
+    {
+      "displayName": "Inventory-Taker"
+    }
+    ```
+
+1. Select **Run query** and confirm **201 Created**. Record the UTC time, response `request-id`, any returned `client-request-id`, and returned application's object `id` for cleanup.
+1. Repeat with `displayName` set to `Sales-Inventory-Taker`. Confirm **201 Created** and record the time, request identifiers, and object `id` separately.
+1. Select **GET** and enter the following URL. Replace the placeholder with one recorded request ID and the timestamps with a UTC window that includes the request. The start and end times are inclusive:
+
+    ```http
+    https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/auditLogs/resourcePolicy?$filter=requestId eq '{request-id-or-client-request-id}' and evaluatedDateTime ge 2026-11-06T09:00:00Z and evaluatedDateTime le 2026-11-06T18:00:00Z&$select=id,requestId,policyDecision,policyDetails
+    ```
+
+1. Select **Run query**.
+1. Find `enforce_application_name_prefix` in `policyDetails` and confirm `policyVersion` is `1.0.0`. If no event matches the response `request-id`, try the returned `client-request-id`. Allow for logging delay; no event isn't proof of compliance.
+1. Repeat the query for the other recorded request and compare the results below.
+
+| Application name | Expected assignment detail in report-only mode |
+| --- | --- |
+| `Inventory-Taker` | `isApplicable: true`, `isCompliant: false`, `isEnforced: false`, and a naming explanation in `policyMessage`. |
+| `Sales-Inventory-Taker` | `isApplicable: true`, `isCompliant: true`, and `isEnforced: false`. |
+
+Check that `policyLoadingError`, `applicabilityEvaluationError`, and `evaluationError` are null or absent. Treat errors separately from a successfully evaluated violation.
+
+These two requests don't measure the policy's impact on all production traffic. For a production rollout, [assess representative traffic](resource-policy-logs.md#assess-assignment-impact-from-evaluation-events) and follow [safe deployment practices](resource-policy-safe-deployment.md). The preview doesn't provide aggregated impact reports.
+
+## 3. Enforce the policy
+
+1. Browse to **Tenant governance** > **Assignments** and open `enforce_application_name_prefix`.
+1. On **Assignment details**, select **Edit**.
+1. On **Settings**, keep **Status** set to **On** and change **Enforcement** from **Report-only** to **Enforce**.
+1. On **Parameters**, keep `Engineering-`, `Marketing-`, `IT-`, `HR-`, `Finance-`, and `Sales-` in `allowed_departments`. Leave `banned_word_list` and `client_appid_exclusion_list` empty.
+1. On **Review**, review the summary and select **Save**.
+1. Reopen **Assignment details** and confirm **Status** is **On** and **Enforcement** is **Enforce**.
+
+Wait for [assignment changes to propagate](resource-policy-evaluation.md#assignment-propagation), then use Graph Explorer to test enforcement. The noncompliant name should be blocked; the compliant name should create an application.
+
+### Test a noncompliant request
+
+Try to create an application with a name that doesn't start with an allowed prefix.
+
+1. In Graph Explorer, select **POST** and **beta**, and enter this request URL:
+
+    ```http
+    https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/applications
+    ```
+
+1. In **Request Body**, enter:
+
+    ```json
+    {
+      "displayName": "Inventory-Taker"
+    }
+    ```
+
+1. Select **Run query**.
+1. In **Response preview**, confirm **403 Forbidden** with `error.code` set to `DeniedByResourcePolicy`. The error message identifies assignment `enforce_application_name_prefix` and explains that the application name needs an allowed department prefix.
+
+Inspect the response body rather than relying on Graph Explorer's generic permissions message for a **403** response. The `DeniedByResourcePolicy` code, assignment identifier, and naming reason identify the policy denial in this example.
+
+### Test a compliant request
+
+Use the same application-creation URL with a name that starts with an allowed prefix.
+
+1. Keep **POST**, **beta**, and the same request URL.
+1. In **Request Body**, enter:
+
+    ```json
+    {
+      "displayName": "Sales-Inventory-Taker"
+    }
+    ```
+
+1. Select **Run query**.
+1. In **Response preview**, confirm **201 Created** and copy the returned application's `id` for cleanup. Use the object `id`, not the `appId`.
+
+## 4. Return to report-only and verify recovery
+
+To stop blocking requests without removing the assignment, return it to report-only mode.
+
+1. Open **Assignment details** for `enforce_application_name_prefix` and select **Edit**.
+1. On **Settings**, keep **Status** set to **On** and change **Enforcement** to **Report-only**. Leave the parameters unchanged.
+1. On **Review**, select **Save**.
+1. Reopen **Assignment details** and confirm **On** and **Report-only**.
+1. Wait for [assignment changes to propagate](resource-policy-evaluation.md#assignment-propagation).
+1. In Graph Explorer, repeat **POST** to `https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/applications` with `displayName` set to `Inventory-Taker`. Expect **201 Created** unless another control blocks it, and record the returned object's `id` for cleanup.
+
+Confirm recovery with the real request, not just the saved setting or a simulated evaluation. Report-only continues to evaluate the assignment but doesn't enforce its deny effect.
+
+## 5. Clean up
+
+Remove the assignment retained from the quickstart and clean up only the test resources you created.
+
+### Remove the assignment
+
+Delete the assignment from the tenant-wide list.
+
+1. Browse to **Tenant governance** > **Assignments**.
+1. Select the checkbox for `enforce_application_name_prefix`. Confirm that only the intended assignment is selected, including any selections hidden by the current filter.
+1. Select **Delete**.
+1. In **Remove assignment?**, confirm **Selected items: 1.**, then select **Delete**.
+
+Deleting the assignment stops it from applying the policy and moves it to **Deleted items**. You can restore it for 30 days.
+
+### Remove the test applications
+
+Remove every application created by the report-only, enforcement, and recovery tests. More than one application can have the same display name. Use each object's `id` returned by a successful creation request to identify the test resource, not its `appId` or display name alone.
+
+1. In the Microsoft Entra admin center, go to **Entra ID** > **App registrations** and select a test application.
+1. On the application's **Overview** page, confirm its object ID matches one recorded during this tutorial, then select **Delete**.
+1. In **Delete app registration**, review the warning that the app won't be able to sign in users or access protected resources, then select **Delete**.
+1. Open **Notifications** and confirm the deletion succeeded for that application.
+1. Repeat for each remaining test application whose object ID you recorded.
+
+## Next steps
+
+For a production rollout, use [Safely deploy resource policy assignments](resource-policy-safe-deployment.md) to plan representative observation, application-owner review, and recovery.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Quickstart: Assign and test a built-in resource policy](resource-policy-quickstart-portal.md).
+- [Analyze resource policy evaluation audit logs](resource-policy-logs.md).
+- [Create and manage resource policies in the Microsoft Entra admin center](resource-policy-manage-portal.md).
+- [Update and retire resource policies](resource-policy-lifecycle.md).

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Entra ID: Risk-based anti-bot verification (CAPTCHA) for SMS and voice multi-factor authentication
messageCenterItems.summary: Starting mid-November 2026, Microsoft Entra ID will add risk-based CAPTCHA verification for SMS and voice MFA to prevent automated fraud. Some users may need to complete CAPTCHA before receiving codes or calls. Administrators should prepare users, ensure network readiness, and promote phishing-resistant methods.
messageCenterItems.body:
What and why

Microsoft Entra ID is adding safeguards to protect telephony-based multifactor authentication (MFA) from automated fraudulent activity. Some users who use SMS or voice for MFA may be asked to complete a risk-based anti-bot verification step (CAPTCHA) before Microsoft sends an SMS verification code or initiates a verification call.

This change is separate from the planned retirement of SMS and voice authentication and does not affect the retirement timeline.

Rollout schedule

  • Worldwide: Beginning in mid-November 2026.

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Users who use SMS or voice for Microsoft Entra ID multifactor authentication

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Entra ID
  • SMS and voice authentication methods

What will happen

  • Some users may be prompted to complete a risk-based anti-bot verification step (CAPTCHA) before Microsoft sends an SMS verification code or initiates a verification call.
  • The verification step will appear only for authentication attempts that meet sufficiently high-risk thresholds.
  • Users with restrictive network or firewall settings may be unable to complete SMS or voice MFA if the verification experience cannot load.

Action required and recommendations

We recommend that administrators take the following actions:

  • Prepare your help desk and notify users that some SMS and voice MFA attempts may require an additional CAPTCHA verification step.
  • Review the risk-based anti-bot verification documentation for network-readiness guidance. If your organization uses restrictive firewalls, proxies, or web filtering, ensure that the required resources can load during authentication.
  • Continue moving users to phishing-resistant authentication methods, such as passkeys, where possible.

Learn more

  • Passkeys by default and retirement of Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication - Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn
  • Risk-based anti-bot verification (CAPTCHA) for telephony-based sign-in - Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn
  • Understanding telephony fraud risk for Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication - Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.
